title: Journalist Arrested While Documenting Legally Contested Enbridge Line 5 Construction
content:
Ashland County, WI – Police arrested video journalist and Unicorn Riot contributor River Akemann while he was documenting Enbridge Line 5 construction on August 24. He was monitoring fish in a creek where Enbridge lacks necessary authorization to install its pipeline. He received four misdemeanor charges and was released later that day. The charges include disorderly conduct, trespassing, unlawful assembly, and resisting arrest.


Canadian oil giant Enbridge has a secretive deal with Ashland County to reimburse the sheriff’s department to act as private security. Enbridge is paying police using the Wisconsin Counties Association, a lobbying group, as the pass through. The Association is not subject to state open records laws. The public won’t know how much Enbridge is paying law enforcement or how the money is being spent.


Multiple groups are suing Canadian oil giant Enbridge for proceeding with Line 5 construction without required property interests at 49 water crossings. Plaintiffs include the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa and multiple environmental organizations.


Aerial photo of the Bad River. Photo via Devon Cupery, originally

published by WUWM on Aug. 11, 2026

.


On August 14 and 17, water protectors waded in a stream where Enbridge was trenching without necessary authorization. The group held a prayerful presence in the stream and stopped construction for multiple hours. Four individuals received citations for allegedly violating an Ashland County trespassing ordinance with fines totaling $1,500. Public trust law protects access to navigable waterways in the United States. 


Enbridge’s Line 5 pipeline transports 22 million gallons of oil and natural gas liquids each day through the Great Lakes region. The pipeline is 73 years old, operating 20 years beyond its engineered lifespan. Enbridge is pushing to complete a 41-mile Line 5 reroute around the Bad River Reservation in Northern Wisconsin, despite numerous legal challenges. 


On August 25, the older Line 5 ruptured in Saxon, WI,

releasing natural gas liquids

. According to Enbridge, a parked, unoccupied semi truck rolled into an excavation site and struck the pipeline. The spill occurred two miles east of the Bad River Reservation and five miles south of Lake Superior. Line 5 is currently shut down because of the spill. 


Enbridge Line 5 Spills Natural Gas Liquids in Northern Wisconsin


Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers and the DNR have asked Enbridge to stop work on the 41-mile reroute while the agency investigates the spill. DNR Secretary Kathryn Hyun said the agency is “immensely frustrated” by Enbridge’s lack of transparency regarding the spill and other recent noncompliance events.


In 2019, the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa sued Enbridge for illegal trespassing and demanded Enbridge leave their watershed. Several of Enbridge’s easements had expired in 2013, and the Bad River Band refused to renew them, citing the risk of tremendous environmental damage from potential crude oil spills. Enbridge is now rerouting the pipeline directly around the reservation despite objections from the Band. The reroute cuts through hundreds of waterways that flow into the tribe’s extensive coastal wild rice beds. The Bad River Band and environmental groups are suing to stop construction.


The aging Line 5 runs along the bottom of the Straits of Mackinac for four miles, and experts warn that the pipeline is at risk of a catastrophic rupture into the Great Lakes.

title: Como é viver na Alemanha nas eleições que podem entregar governos à AfD
content:
Eu moro na periferia de Berlim, em um conjunto habitacional construído para os trabalhadores pelo governo comunista

, na época em que a cidade ainda era dividida por um muro. São prédios grandes, de arquitetura brutalista, com muitos apartamentos, que rodeiam praças com bastante verde. 


Por serem condomínios geridos por cooperativas, longe do centro e com valor de aluguel baixo, o bairro todo é naturalmente composto por uma maioria de imigrantes.

Como em quase toda metrópole, os imigrantes, pessoas com trabalhos informais e com baixos salários são empurradas para as bordas, ou no caso de Berlim, para fora do “Ring”

, como falamos aqui, já que a cidade tem o formato de um anel.


No último fim de semana eu caminhava pelo bairro, prestando atenção aos diferentes idiomas que ouvia: russo, chinês, inglês, quando

notei um cartaz preso bem alto, em um poste de luz. “Migração precisa de Fronteira”, escrito em tons de azul, assinado pelo partido de extrema direita Alternativa para Alemanha, AfD na sigla em alemão. Alguns passos à frente outro cartaz do partido: “Deportar imigrantes criminosos”. E outro: “Na escola, o alemão é mandatório”.

 O bairro todo estava tomado por essas mensagens. 


Agora, em meados de setembro acontecem eleições estaduais em Saxônia-Anhalt, Berlim e Mecklemburgo-Pomerânia Ocidental, além de eleições municipais na Baixa Saxônia, e por isso as propagandas políticas estão por toda a parte.

Mas não é apenas irônico – pelo passado comunista deste pedaço – como muito violento que a AfD tenha escolhido esses slogans para espalhar pelo meu bairro. 


Não é propaganda eleitoral, é um recado. 


“Deportar migrantes criminosos”


“Na escola, o alemão é obrigatório”


“Migração Precisa de Fronteiras”


A AfD tem se tornado cada vez mais radical em seus discursos, ao mesmo tempo em que cresce vertiginosamente nas pesquisas.

 Desde as eleições federais que elegeram o chanceler Friedrich Merz da União Democrata Cristã (CDU) em 2025, a principal pauta do partido tem sido a deportação em massa como solução mágica para a crise política, econômica e o aumento na criminalidade. “Deportar aos milhares”, cantavam jovens alemães em comícios do partido, que ficou em segundo lugar naquelas eleições.


No fim do ano passado, eu me infiltrei em um evento da AfD na Turíngia

, que fazia um “balanço” dos 10 anos desde que a ex-chanceler Angela Merkel “abriu as porteiras” do país aos refugiados, como eles dizem. Logo na entrada, uma pasta com uma longa lista de nacionalidades e porcentagem de crimes cometidos na Alemanha era entregue aos participantes. No telão, fotos de criminosos árabes procurados pela polícia rodavam em looping.

Na plateia lotada, alemães de todas as idades aplaudiam e gritavam por deportações e pelo fim do multiculturalismo.


E com esse tom cada vez mais violento e ultranacionalista, na Saxônia-Anhalt,

o partido está com 43% das intenções de voto para as eleições de 6 de setembro.


“Vamos formar o governo na Saxônia-Anhalt”, disse a co-líder do partido, Alice Weidel, em entrevista à emissora pública ZDF.

Até hoje, a AfD ainda não conseguiu entrar em um governo estadual ou federal porque todos os outros principais partidos descartaram cooperar com o partido extremista, algo que ficou conhecido como “cordão sanitário”. 


O problema é que esse cordão dá sinais de desgaste.

 Primeiro porque, como aconteceu no Brasil com o PSDB, os partidos de direita clássica e centro direita estão perdendo cada vez mais espaço nos parlamentos e já esboçam abraçar pautas mais radicais para cair no gosto dos eleitores. 


Segundo que, em um governo que precisa de coalizões, a manobra para evitar a AfD está se tornando cada vez mais complicada. Nas eleições federais, por exemplo, como a Alemanha tem regime parlamentarista, o partido de Merz precisou “pular” a AfD que ficou em segundo lugar e fazer coligações com dois outros partidos menores para governar – foi um processo super delicado e demorado. 


Por último, essas eleições regionais contam com algumas novidades, sobretudo na Saxônia. Com vários partidos menores obtendo resultados próximos ao limite eleitoral de 5% na Alemanha, a AfD pode ter uma maioria absoluta das cadeiras e seu principal candidato, Ulrich Siegmund, poderá se tornar o primeiro governador de um estado alemão a ocupar o cargo desde a fundação do partido em 2013.

content:

El fascista Alejandro Sarubbi Benítez asegura que maneja “todo lo que hace acá” el exasesor de Milei y creador de La Derecha Diario que ahora está preso por intentar matar a su pareja. ¿Qué sabe de los hechos y cómo encubre a su “cliente” el stramer que desde la cloaca Carajo destila mensajes de odio y violencia? ¿Podría ser imputado por encubridor?

Por Daniel Satur (La Izquierda Diario).


Desde la medianoche del viernes el 

operador mediático-digital de la ultraderecha latinoamericana

 

Fernando Cerimedo

Bolivia

otra causa contra Cerimedo

“enriquecimiento ilícito”

, ya que en varios allanamientos a sus propiedades en el país vecino se secuestraron 

grandes sumas de dinero

 sin justificar y material más que comprometedor.


Como lo definió 

Fernando Rosso

 en 

su editorial del sábado

, 

Cerimedo

 “encaja bastante bien” como símbolo de

 esa 

lumpen-casta

 

que la ultraderecha continental creó

 a partir del rejunte de “empresarios quebrados, periodistas de dudosa reputación, subcelebridades, 

traders

, 

coaches

 mediocres, policías, militares e influencers que encontraron en la radicalización política la posibilidad de una nueva carrera, no para progresar, sino para trepar”. Ahí están también 

Manuel Adorni

 y 

José Luis Espert

, claro.


En Argentina, parte de esa 

troupe

 que acompaña al Gobierno de 

Javier Milei

“influencers”

 que a diario destilan violencia y odio a través de sitios como 

La Derecha Diario

 

y canales como 

Carajo Stream

 

. Personajes por demás crípticos que conviven, transan y comparten negocios dentro de un mismo ecosistema mal llamado libertario.


Por caso, el pasquín de 

fake news

 (creado para la “batalla cultural” contra 

La Izquierda Diario

) fue cofundado por le mismo 

Cerimedo

 y su esposa 

Natalia Basil

; mientras que en el canal de 

Youtube

Daniel “Gordo Dan” Parisini

 despunta el vicio comunicacional el abogado 

Alejandro Sarubbi Benítez

, conocido en redes como 

“Gordo Leyes”

 y nada menos que defendor en Argentina de 

Cerimedo

.


En línea con el estilo libertariano, a

Indio Solari

Nadia Beller horas después del atentado contra su vida | Captura de video


“Unas complicaciones”


Sarubbi Benítez

 conduce en 

Carajo

 el programa 

La Trinchera

. El jueves de la semana pasada, cuando

 

su amigo ya llevaba dos días y medio detenido en Santa Cruz de la Sierra, habló por primera vez del tema. Usó unos pocos segundos para decir que venía de 

días complicados

 y con “dolor de cuello” por “todo el quilombo 

Cerimedo

”. Y agregó: “No es ningún misterio que yo 

soy abogado de él acá

, lo que significa básicamente 

asumir yo todo lo que él hace acá

 y eso trae unas complicaciones”. Claramente, los une algo más que una mera relación profesional de letrado-cliente.


Fingiendo serenidad, el

Desde su cuenta de

author: dev
title: Archéologie d'un vrai-faux silence : Michel Foucault, Israël et les Palestiniens [3/3]
content:
Inspirés de longue date par le travail de Michel Foucault

 [

1

]

, les philosophes Alain Brossat et Alain Naze ont enquêté sur le « vrai-faux silence » de l'intellectuel préféré des français autour de la Palestine et d'Israël. La première partie de ce travail est accessible

ici

, la seconde

là

.


On a pu discerner déjà, dans les développements précédents, toute l'importance que revêtent les associations subreptices et les enchaînements tacites, dans l'établissement d'une position durable qui ne s'explicite pas sur un mode plein, mais demeure toujours en creux et ne s'expose au grand jour que par intermittences, « au détour d'une conversation » - ou d'une intervention écrite. Ces passages à l'explicite prennent la forme de « sorties », dans la plus parfaite des discontinuités et c'est donc à ses propres risques que l'enquêteur tente de rétablir de la continuité là où ne sont demeurés que des pointillés, très espacés. Le Petit Poucet Foucault ne nous a pas, ici, facilité la tâche, les petits cailloux blancs qui balisent son parcours dans la forêt (sombre) du conflit israélo-palestinien sont rares et souvent bien cachés. Exemple : dans l'un de ses cours au Collège de France (« Il faut défendre la société »), Foucault affirme (un peu hâtivement) que le socialisme, tant comme doctrine que comme pratique étatique, débouche nécessairement sur le racisme

 [

2

]

. Cette simplification a comme effet que la campagne exterminationniste entreprise par Staline contre les « koulaks » peut être associée aux différentes éruptions d'antisémitisme sous le règne de Staline, notamment l'affaire des « blouses blanches » évoquée plus haut. Du coup se trouve renforcée la suture qui, pour Foucault, rend indissociables l'hostilité au communisme à la soviétique et le philosémitisme alimentant la sympathie pour Israël.


Un nouveau nœud de même espèce se forme à l'occasion de l'Affaire Croissant, en 1977. Klaus Croissant, avocat de la défense lors du procès de la Fraction Armée Rouge (« Bande à Baader ») venait de demander l'asile en France, se réclamant de l'article de la Constitution de 1946, garantissant l'asile à quiconque est persécuté pour ses actions en faveur de la liberté. Mais Croissant était poursuivi en Allemagne sous l'inculpation d'association à une entreprise criminelle – celle de la RAF. De ce fait même, il pouvait se trouver exclu du bénéfice de l'asile. Cependant, comme le relève David Macey, pour ceux qui en France le soutenaient, « son véritable crime avait été d'attirer l'attention sur les conditions de détention dans la prison-forteresse de Stammheim » et qui, en octobre 1977, avaient amplement contribuer à pousser Andreas Baader, Gudrun Ennslin et Jan-Karle Raspe à se suicider. De fait, la décision du Procureur de Karlsruhe d'exclure de Croissant de la défense d'Andreas Baader se fondait sur l'affirmation que l'avocat a « pris part à l'élaboration de l'interview au magazine

 Spiegel

, interview qui fait clairement partie de la lutte révolutionnaire que les accusés continuent de mener de leur détention ». Or, comme le fait remarquer Klaus Croissant, les propos tenus par les prisonniers, et repris dans cette publication, « traduisent la définition politique que la R.A.F. (Fraction Armée Rouge) s'est donnée » ; par conséquent, le fait de « présenter cette définition à l'opinion publique avant le procès est l'un des devoirs de la défense et un droit des accusés » - d'où il suit que le tribunal n'était pas compétent « pour censurer les questions posées par le

Spiegel

 et les réponses données par les accusés »

 [

3

]

.


« Croissant, poursuit Macey, avait déjà fait deux séjours en prison ; on lui avait confisqué son passeport et obligation lui avait été faite de se présenter toutes les semaines au poste de police. Désormais incapable de se défendre en Allemagne, il avait choisi l'exil et espéré poursuivre ses activités en France »

 [

4

]

.


Arrêté fin septembre à Paris, il se trouvait alors sous le coup d'une procédure d'extradition. S'ensuivit une mobilisation impulsée par un groupe de personnalités, exigeant la libération de l'avocat, se réclamant d'une longue tradition en matière de droit d'asile pour des motifs politiques. Foucault ne figurait pas parmi les signataires (Simone de Beauvoir, Sartre, Maurice Clavel, Gilles Deleuze, François Sagan, Georges Kiejman...) mais, selon Macey, « il n'en fut pas moins actif, alors, de diverses autres manières »

 [

5

]

. Parmi celles-ci, un article paru …

author: Kelly Hayes
title: “Woke 1” Narratives Suggest the US Was Briefly Ruled by the Left. It Wasn’t.
content:
The US wasn’t remade according to abolitionist or socialist movement demands. Now fascists wield the machinery of power.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The political pendulum swings, and some people are getting caught up in its momentum. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has been reasonably criticized for her giggly embrace of attacks on “Woke 1” — a made-up era of US politics some commentators are now demanding “accountability” for.

The “Woke 1” framing suggests that the United States was briefly ruled by the left. This fantasy erases MAGA from a moment in history when they controlled the levers of government and terrorized their opponents and those they had scapegoated for a moment of national crisis. In 2020, we saw armed protests against COVID mitigations, attacks on health care workers, the mass amplification of conspiracy theories, Trump’s “LIBERATE” tweets, escalating election denial, and the political trajectory that produced an attempted coup on January 6.

It’s true that 2020 was a year of extremes. Experiencing organized abandonment, being pent up at home to ponder the situation, and living much of our political lives in contentious digital spaces contributed to some rather intense pronouncements and actions. This was true on the right and the left. For many Americans, the murder of George Floyd was a flashpoint — one that demanded a reckoning. Calls for reimagining the social order, including abolishing the police, gained traction. And while some were envisioning a world without rampant state violence, where people’s identities were respected and their basic needs met, others were embracing very different forms of radicalization.

Historically, pandemics have been followed by increased social unrest and political upheaval. Many of us hoped this particular rupture might function as a portal, as Arundhati Roy suggested, opening the way for a leftward shift. For a time, this seemed possible.

I have my political disappointments about that period, but they are not about the things many pundits are seizing upon now, as they demand “accountability” for the social repercussions some people endured for racial insensitivity, transphobia, ableism, misogyny, or sex pest behavior — or for toothless corporate policies and mollifying gestures from Democrats that no one on the left asked for.

But whatever missteps people on the left made during that period — for example, some of us may have been too quick to dismiss potential allies we deemed insufficiently radical — our politics did not become the governing politics of the United States. The left did not take power. In fact, many of us lent our momentum to the Biden campaign as a moral compromise to end the Trump regime. The country was not remade according to abolitionist, socialist, or movement demands. Nor did the left lose two elections to a fascist. The Democrats did.

What failed to regain sufficient public support to hold off fascism was the neoliberal status quo. And today, Democrats are still fighting to keep their party’s politics in the center — a position from which they will either continue to lose, or win and then lose, because they ultimately have nothing transformative to offer in a time of increased economic suffering.

Meanwhile, the right continued on its intensified path, ever-radicalizing, until we wound up here.

I am not minimizing the left’s shortcomings. I happen to think leftist Twitter culture, prior to the Elon takeover and sometimes even after, involved a lot of excesses. (Anyone remember the nice lady who made her neighbor chili?) I sometimes engaged in those excesses. (Though not the chili situation.) I was sometimes targeted because of them. (And my god, that shit was ridiculous.) Some leftists, reasonably aghast at Biden’s role in the Gaza genocide, quite unreasonably minimized the threat of a second Trump administration. That was a mistake, and one that aggravated me to no end, but it’s not the mistake we’re being called “crazy” for.

I have come to accept that people don’t always reach the most sensible conclusions in environments designed to amplify rancor and reward conflict, while bombarding people with more bad news and atrocity than their brains were built to process.

People grow, and movements adjust, based on experience and changing conditions. I have learned a lot in recent years, as I hope we all have.

But I want to call attention to what’s been memory-holed …

author: Unknown
title: Women in Batman: The mechanism that covers up femicide must be dismantled
content:
The

I Need Peace Women’s Initiative

 held a statement outside Batman (Êlih) Bar Association for Rojwelat Kızmaz and other women killed as a result of a male-dominated mentality. A banner reading, “What happened to Rojwelat Kızmaz? Femicides must be investigated, perpetrators must be prosecuted,” was displayed.


The Turkish text of the statement was read by Yağmur Alaz Gülveren, a member of the initiative, while the Kurdish text was read by Hava Can, a member of TJA.


What happened to Rojwelat Kızmaz


Drawing attention to the relationship between violence against women and war policies, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren stated that the use of sexual violence as a weapon in wars creates conditions that allow systematic crimes against women to be covered up.


Pointing to the recording of women’s deaths in the region as “suspicious deaths,” Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said: “From a city with a deep memory of violence against women and femicides, and where such violence occurs most frequently as a result of violence by the male-dominated state, in other words, from Batman, we ask: What happened to Rojwelat Kızmaz?”


Why are the suspects not being arrested


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren also raised the case of Ipek Er, who was driven to suicide after being subjected to sexual assault by specialist sergeant Musa Orhan, and criticized the fact that the suspect had not been arrested.


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren asked: “Why has Musa Orhan still not been arrested? Do the inspection reports of the Ministry of Family and Social Services contain any warnings or administrative sanctions against the Private Şifa Care Center?”


Stating that the facts behind the classification of women’s deaths as “suicides” must be brought to light, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said, “Will the real causes of these deaths and the perpetrators be uncovered? For a genuine and lasting peace, will crimes against women be confronted, and will the perpetrators be prosecuted?”


Allegations concerning the Şifa care center


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren stated that male state violence is not limited to femicides and also drew attention to allegations concerning the Private Batman Şifa Care Center.


She said that allegations that a woman at the care center was subjected to systematic sexual assault and underwent two abortions, that people under the center’s care were subjected to torture and mistreatment, and that efforts were made to cover up suspicious deaths must be investigated.


Impunity continues


Drawing attention to a mechanism of impunity in Batman extending from deaths recorded as “female suicides” since the 1990s to femicides in which the perpetrators are known, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren stated that this was not merely a matter of isolated acts of male violence.


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said: “This is not simply the violence of individual men; it is the organized form of male dominance, nourished by the politics of war, spreading across the entire region.”


Stating that Turkey’s security-oriented policies toward the Kurdish issue have a long history, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said that the strengthening of security policies after 2015 “combined special war policies with male dominance and hostility toward women, thereby intensifying forms of violence against women.”


We will continue our struggle for justice


Stating that they would continue their struggle for women’s right to life and freedom, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said they would continue to follow cases that authorities seek to cover up. Yağmur Alaz Gülveren added: “For genuine peace and for women’s freedom, we say an end to special war policies and male state violence.”


The statement ended with applause and chants including “Long live women’s solidarity,” “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (“Women, Life, Freedom”), “Women do not want war, they want peace,” and “Femicide is political.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: Rosario: movilización contra los femicidios y en reclamo de la emergencia en violencia de género
content:
Las organizaciones decidieron movilizarse luego de que se conocieran tres femicidios en 15 días.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Escuchar el reporte de Darío Uliassi desde Aire Libre Radio Comunitaria.


Concentraron este miércoles a las 17 frente a la Municipalidad de Rosario y finalizaron con un acto en la puerta de la sede de Gobernación de la provincia en la ciudad.


De la movilización participaron organizaciones feministas, sociales y políticas que se expresaron en contra de la violencia machista y reclamaron justicia por los femicidios.


En la provincia de Santa Fe se registraron más de 30 femicidios en lo que va del año. Además, se contabilizaron 10 víctimas más que en el mismo período del año pasado.


“Paren de matarnos” fue la consigna que encabezó la movilización donde las organizaciones advirtieron por la suba de casos, que se profundizan con el desmantelamiento de las políticas de género en los distintos niveles del Estado.


En declaraciones a Aire Libre, Gabriela Sosa, referente del movimiento feminista Mujeres por la Matria Latinoamericana (Mumalá), exigió la sanción de una ley provincial que declare la emergencia en violencia de género y que se cumpla la ordenanza local que declaró la emergencia hace un tiempo.


“Hemos presentado proyectos para que se declare la emergencia en violencia de género en Santa Fe y también que se pueda aplicar aquella ordenanza de hace varios años que ya declaraba la emergencia en Rosario y que disponía de recursos que siguen estando pendientes”.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Sosa también denunció las consecuencias del desmantelamiento de políticas públicas: “Esta quita de recursos, a la par de los discursos de odios, comienzan a impactar que las mujeres cada vez denunciamos menos, un 9% de la víctimas habían denunciado a su agresor anteriormente”.


Y agregó: “Por supuesto faltan campañas de prevención, faltan que los medios de comunicación tengan pautas de los estados municipales, provinciales y nacionales para informar de qué hacer”.

author: Rizomatica
title: Llenado del embalse de la central hidroeléctrica Los Lagos, un reconocimiento expreso de la violación a la debida diligencia por parte de Statkraft
content:
La confirmación de Statkraft refuerza la urgencia y la pertinencia de la queja presentada por el Aylla Rewe del Ngen Mapu Kintuantü ante las autoridades noruegas por posibles incumplimientos de las obligaciones de debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos.


COMUNICADO DE PRENSA.


«Territorio del Pilmaykén, 26 de agosto de 2026. – Como Aylla Rewe del Ngen Mapu Kintuantü, recibimos con profunda preocupación la confirmación formal por parte de Statkraft de que concluyó el llenado del embalse del proyecto hidroeléctrico Los Lagos, en la cuenca del río Pilmaiquén.


Durante años hemos advertido públicamente sobre las consecuencias que este proyecto puede tener para nuestros derechos como pueblo Mapuche Williche, nuestra relación con el territorio, nuestra espiritualidad, nuestra cultura, nuestra memoriay nuestras formas de vida.


También es información pública que, dentro del territorio involucrado, existen espacios de profundo significado espiritual y cultural para nuestro pueblo y que en la zona se realizaron hallazgos arqueológicos y bioantropológicos de los cuales la empresa tenía conocimiento.


La empresa y las autoridades conocían estas preocupaciones antes de que se completara el llenado del embalse. Aun asi, la empresa decidió seguir adelante. La confirmación del llenado del embalse es una prueba flagrante de la violación a los estándares de debida diligencia corporativa en materia de derechos humanos y de la desatención a las voces y llamados reiterados de las comunidades.


Esta confirmación no resta importancia a las acciones legales que hemos impulsado. Por el contrario, confirma precisamente la urgencia y pertinencia de la queja que presentamos hace unas semanas ante la Autoridad de Consumo de Noruega, con el acompañamiento legal del Proyecto de Derechos Económicos, Sociales y Culturales (ProDESC) y de la Iniciativa para la Justicia Transnacional. (IJT), en la que solicitamos que se investigue si Statkraft cumplió adecuadamente con sus obligaciones de debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos.


Para nosotros, trasladar elementos materiales no sustituye ni repara la relación espiritual, cultural y territorial de la que forman parte.


Como Aylla Rewe, hemos utilizado durante años las distintas vías legales e institucionales disponibles para exigir el respeto a nuestros derechos y que Statkraft cumpla con su obligación de debida diligencia.

Hemos participado e impulsado procesos relacionados con la consulta indígena, recurrido a instancias judiciales nacionales y presentado una queja ante el Punto Nacional de Contacto de Noruega por posibles incumplimientos de las Líneas Directrices de la OCDE para Empresas Multinacionales.


Ante la ausencia de una respuesta capaz de prevenir las afectaciones que veníamos advirtiendo, hace unas semanas nos vimos obligados a acudir nuevamente a las propias instituciones noruegas y presentar una queja al amparo de la Ley de Transparencia.

No llegamos a esta instancia como primera opción.

Llegamos después de años de utilizar mecanismos legales e institucionales para exigir que nuestros derechos fueran respetados antes de que el territorio fuera transformado.


Por eso, la confirmación del llenado del embalse vuelve la queja aún más urgente.

La debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos no puede reducirse a cumplir procedimientos formales o a elaborar informes. Su función sustantiva es identificar los  riesgos, prevenir sus impactos, mitigarlos y actuar antes de que las afectaciones se materialicen.


Lo informado refuerza nuestra preocupación de que las advertencias de las comunidades y los riesgos para nuestros derechos no hayan sido atendidos de manera efectiva antes de que el proyecto avanzara y produjera transformaciones materiales en el territorio.


Ahora estamos documentando y verificando directamente el alcance de las afectaciones derivadas del llenado. Sin embargo, este proceso es sumamente complejo, pues, como es de público conocimiento, las comunidades no tienen acceso al sitio de construcción de la Central Los Lagos ni a sus zonas aledañas, ya que el área está resguardada por guardias privados de la empresa y por tanquetas apostadas en los caminos.


Esta situación confirma nuevamente que nuestro derecho de acceso a la información y a la participación en las decisiones que afectan nuestro territorio ha sido sistemáticamente vulnerado: ni las autoridades ni la empresa han garantizado su pleno ejercicio. Resulta especialmente grave que …

Campaigners say anti-rights movements are increasingly using family law to challenge women’s rights to inheritance, property, divorce and child custody.

NAIROBI, Aug 13 2026 (IPS) – Women’s rights advocates, judges and lawyers have launched a coordinated campaign to reform family laws that discriminate against women and girls in Africa.

While the past decade has brought important legal advances in some countries, progress has also been marked by stagnation and backsliding. Increasingly, influential and often well-resourced and highly coordinated anti-rights actors are promoting regressive conservative ideologies that seek to repeal existing legal protections and obstruct reforms that would strengthen rights for women and girls.

Family law governs some of the most consequential aspects of daily life, including marriage, divorce, child custody, inheritance and property rights. Although national constitutions and regional human rights treaties guarantee many protections for women and girls, those guarantees are often undermined by discriminatory legislation, conflicting customary and statutory laws, and weak implementation.

Rights advocates warn that family law has become a key target for coordinated anti-rights campaigns that promote restrictive interpretations of family, gender roles and “traditional values”, because shaping who has rights within the family sets the framework for whose rights are ultimately recognised and protected across society.

“They understand that if you control the family, you control society,” said Irene Mbengue, senior legal officer in the office of the African Commission’s special rapporteur on the rights of women in Africa, in remarks delivered on behalf of Commissioner Janet Ramatoulie Sallah-Njie at the inaugural Africa Family Law Network conference, held in Nairobi, Kenya, from August 4 to 6, 2026.

“If you define who counts as family, who has rights within the family, and who gets to make decisions in the family, you shift the entire social order.”

That struggle is playing out in Uganda, where rights advocates say proposed changes to marriage law could leave many divorced women with little claim to the assets built up over years spent raising children, running households and supporting their families.

Jackie Bless Pinyoloya, Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa (SIHA) Uganda country coordinator, explained that the bill does not guarantee equal division of assets acquired during marriage and leaves women to prove the value of unpaid care work when claiming their share.

“At the point of divorce, a woman is told she only leaves with what she financially contributed… But who counts the years she spent caring for the family?” she said.

Pinyoloya said weak enforcement of existing protections also left women vulnerable, with domestic violence cases often being resolved informally by families or community leaders rather than through courts, while low penalties failed to deter perpetrators.

Equality Now’s 2024 regional study on African family laws in 20 African countries found that this tension over marital assets extends beyond Uganda. In countries including Kenya, Nigeria and Tanzania, judicial insistence on proving direct financial contribution routinely penalises homemakers, while courts struggle to place economic value on unpaid care work.

title: Cinsiyetçi Teknik Direktör'e tepki
content:
Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu 1'nci liginde oynayan Muğlaspor'un geçtiğimiz günlerde basınla tanışma toplantısı vardı. Toplantıda Teknik Direktör Yalçın Koşukavak'ın kadın gazetecilere yönelik cinsiyetçi sözleri tepki topladı. Muğlaspor Teknik Direktörü Yalçın Koşukavak’ın kadın gazetecilere yönelik “Bilsem kısırımı da altınımı da alırdım, gün yapardık” ve “Sizde şimdi soru da yoktur” sözlerine kadın gazeteciler ve kadın örgütleri tepki gösterdi. Muğlaspor Kulübü ise sözlerin “espri amacı taşıdığını” ve bağlamından koparıldığını savundu.


Muğlaspor Teknik Direktörü Yalçın Koşukavak ile 20 Ağustos’ta Muğla’nın Akyaka Mahallesi’nde futbolcular, aileleri, teknik heyet ve basın mensuplarının katıldığı bir kahvaltı etkinliği düzenlendi. Toplantının başında kulüp başkanı ve yöneticiler mekandan ayrıldı. Koşukavak'ın basın toplantısı için hazırlık yapılırken gazetecilerin oturduğu masa teknik direktör için hazırlanmaya başladı. 


Kahvaltığı basın toplantısını 7 kadın ve 4 erkek muhabir takip ediyordu. Koşukavak, sözlerine "Daha önce basın toplantısında bu kadar bayan görmemiştim. Sizde şimdi soru da yoktur. Bilsem kısırımı da altınımı da alırdım, gün yapardık" diyerek başladı.


Etkinlikte yaşananları Mabolla Medya muhabiri Esma Turan; Koşukavak’ın sözlerini ise Bodrum Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nden Figan Erozan ve Evrim İnan bianet’e değerlendirdi.


Turan: Bu sözleri 'espri' olarak değerlendirmiyorum


Mabolla Medya muhabiri Esma Turan, kahvaltı etkinliğinde bulunan kadın gazetecilerden biriydi. Etkinlik öncesi ve sırasında yaşananları anlatan Turan şöyle konuştu:


“Toplantı öncesinde kulüp başkanı, yöneticiler ve futbolcular ile kahvaltı yapıldı. Kahvaltı sonrasında sadece hocanın açıklama yapacağı söylendi. Aslında bir tanışma ve değerlendirme toplantısıydı. Yalçın Bey ile ilk basın toplantısı ve tanışma olacaktı. Kulüp başkanı ve yönetimi mekândan ayrıldı. Bizim masamız basın açıklaması için hazırlanıyordu. Biz mikrofonları hazırlarken hoca geldi, daha masaya oturmadan ve merhaba bile demeden kısır muhabbetini yaptı.”


Turan’ın aktardığına göre gazeteciler önce ne olduğunu anlamadı, ardından “Biz de gün yapmıyoruz burada” diyerek tepki gösterdi. Bunun üzerine Koşukavak, “Sizde soru da yoktur şimdi” dedi.


Turan, toplantıda yaşananları şöyle anlattı:


“Biz de kaldık, dinledik açıkçası. Ne yapacağımızı bilemedik yani kal geldi o sırada galiba. Sonradan keşke kalkıp gitseydik dedik. Sorularımız vardı, onları da sormadık. Erkek meslektaşlarımız da soru sormadı. Sadece Yalçın Bey konuştu. 7 kadın ve 4 erkekti gazeteciler.”


Tepkilerin toplantı sonrasında gazetecilerin kendi aralarındaki değerlendirmeleri ve konunun haberleştirilmesiyle ortaya çıktığını belirten Turan, “Haber yapmasalar olur mu? Kulübe zarar gelmesin, cumartesi maç var” denildiğini söyledi.


Koşukavak’ı kişisel olarak hedef almak veya Muğlaspor’a zarar vermek gibi bir amaçlarının olmadığını vurgulayan Turan şöyle devam etti:


“Muğlaspor, bu şehrin önemli bir değeri ve hepimiz kulübün başarılı olmasını istiyoruz. Biz orada söylenen sözleri duyduğumuz şekliyle, kayda geçtiği biçimiyle kamuoyuna aktardık.”


Muğlaspor Kulübü’nün olayın ardından yayımladığı açıklamaya katılmadığını belirten Turan, “Sizde şimdi soru da yoktur” ifadesini kadınların mesleki yeterliliğini ve gazetecilik mesleğini cinsiyet üzerinden değerlendiren bir yaklaşım olarak yorumladı.


Kadınları kamusal alandan dışlayan bir pratik


Bodrum Kadın Dayanışma Derneği de sosyal medya hesabından Koşukavak’ın sözlerine ilişkin bir açıklama yayımladı.


Açıklamada, “Bunu bir kişinin nezaketsizliği olarak değil, erkek egemen kurumların kadınları kamusal alandan dışlama pratiği olarak görüyoruz” denildi.


Koşukavak’ın “kısır” ve “altın günü” ifadelerine de tepki gösterilen açıklamada şöyle denildi:


“‘Kısır’ ve ‘altın günü’ üzerinden kurulan alay, kadınların dayanışma pratiklerini ve mesleki kimliklerini aynı anda küçümsemektedir.”


Muğla Barosu ve Menteşe Kadın Platformu: Münferit bir şaka değil


Menteşe Kadın Platformu ile Muğla Barosu Kadın Hakları ve Toplumsal Cinsiyet Eşitliği Komisyonu da Koşukavak’ın ifadelerine ilişkin ortak bir açıklama yayımladı.


Açıklamada Koşukavak’ın sözlerinin “münferit bir şaka” olmadığı belirtilerek şöyle denildi:


“Bu söylem; sporu, basını ve kamusal alanı yalnızca erkeklere ait gören, kadını ev içi rollerle, geleneksel kalıplarla ve edilgenlikle tanımlamaya çalışan ataerkil zihniyetin yansımasıdır.”

author: Freedom Shop Aotearoa
title: bell hooks On Patriarchy
content:
This article is presented as two imposed PDFs intended to be printed on A4 paper, resulting in an A5 saddle-stitched pamphlet. The first PDF is a single-sided cover intended to be printed in colour, the second double-sided inside pages intended to be printed in black and white.

bell hooks (1952 – 2021) was born into a working class family in a small town in Kentucky. She published around 40 books ranging from childrens’ stories and cultural commentary to poetry and essays on race, class and gender, becoming known as one of the best US radical writers of recent times. This pamphlet compiles her classic essay Understanding Patriarchy and transcripts of three interviews from 1994, 2011 and 2015. In these interviews, hooks discusses the nature of the patriarchy, the growth of white supremacy in the US, the need for love, the role of humour, spirituality and intersectionality, and the difficuties of remaining relevant when immersed in the academic world. Hooks’ anger, warmth and humanity is evident in these interviews, and reading them makes you feel very annoyed that she’s dead, and you are never going to have the chance to talk to her in person. Given that, I’m afraid this is as good as it gets. Her writing is pretty damn cool, though.

author: Corey Larocque
title: No woman should face harassment from taxi drivers
content:
It’s tragic that Iqaluit women feel the need to consider alternatives to taxis out of fear for their safety but it’s great they’re standing up for themselves.


Next week, Rosalie DeMaio, a Nunavut Arctic College student, is hosting a community meeting so people can discuss how to develop alternatives so they don’t have to rely on taxis.


Women routinely face unwanted come-ons from drivers, she said in an

interview

 with a Nunatsiaq News reporter. (The news story about her concerns is on page 3 of this week’s paper).


DeMaio said a driver once called her “baby girl” when he asked about her night out at a bar. He offered her wine. She declined, saying she just wanted to go to bed.


He persisted.


“I said, ‘No, I want to go to bed.’ And he said, ‘You can go to my bed,'” DeMaio said, adding she has also been followed or watched after being dropped off.


The yuck factor of that story is off the charts.


No woman should be subjected to that kind of advance, but especially not while making use of what’s almost an essential public service.


It’s inappropriate, whether it’s when a woman is taking a taxi to the grocery store or home after going out for a drink with some friends.


Taxis are a vital part of how Iqalummiut get around. The service needs to be safe and reliable for everyone.


The number of people who attend DeMaio’s community meeting on Thursday at the YWCA-Agvik women’s shelter at 7:30 p.m. will be telling. It could give some indication how widespread this issue is.


Both the taxi company and the City of Iqaluit should take note of what’s going on and what people who attend the meeting have to say.


They should have more robust ways of rooting out offensive drivers.


Five years ago, the city’s recently revived public safety committee looked into the issue when taxi drivers were victims of some bored youths who

threw rocks

 at them.


Now, if some drivers are causing problems for Iqaluit women, maybe it’s an issue the

committee

 — which has been looking for

something to do

 — could tackle.


Some of the experiences DeMaio described happened when she took a cab home from a bar. It’s potentially dangerous if women are reluctant to take a taxi home after going out for drinks with a friend. They might choose to drive their own vehicle.


Caribou Cabs manager Rod Mugford said the company has not received a direct complaint from female passengers but has embarked on a human resources program aimed at avoiding problems by training drivers in safety, anti-harassment, sexual misconduct and cultural sensitivity.


Some of DeMaio’s remedies include a women-focused rideshare service, a Facebook group or carpooling app to reduce women’s reliance on taxis.


DeMaio has been looking around for funding to help develop a cellphone app that people could use to co-ordinate their own rideshares.


That should be a no-brainer. Some organization should come to her aid. How much can it cost to develop an app? Some Nunavut organizations have spent money on a lot more trivial things. Give her a little seed money and see if it makes a difference.


Because it’s terrible and unacceptable that women don’t feel safe riding with some taxi drivers.


DeMaio deserves credit for identifying a serious social issue, airing it out and for putting alternatives on the table. That’s how change starts.

title: Wir beziehen Stellung - Ausschluss
content:
Triggerwarnung: Der folgende Text thematisiert sexualisierte Gewalt und kann belastend sein.


Was ist geschehen?


Vor einigen Wochen kam es in unserem Zuhause, einem Wagenplatz in Bern, zum Ausschluss einer Person, welche mehrfach sexuelle Übergriffe und eine Vergewaltigung begangen hat. Jonsi hat etwas mehr als 2 Jahre mit uns gewohnt. Im Sommer 2025 bildete sich nach einem Übergriff eine Bezugsgruppe, welche in Form eines transformativen und gemeinschaftlichen Prozesses versucht hat, Verantwortung zu übernehmen sowie den Raum für Reflexion und Veränderung zu eröffnen. Mit einer gewissen Naivität und Selbstüberschätzung wurde dieser Prozess gestartet. Nach etwa einem halben Jahr des laufenden Aufarbeitungs-Prozesses beging Jonsi eine Vergewaltigung. Wir stellten fest, dass der Prozess weitere sexualisierte Gewalt von Jonsi nicht verhindern konnte.


Dies macht uns wütend und betroffen. Um Personen auf dem Platz zu schützen, und dem fehlenden Vertrauen in den Prozess und die Bereitschaft von Jonsi für diesen Prozess, haben wir uns entschieden Jonsi nicht weiter in unserem Kollektiv mitzutragen.


Wir bewegen uns damit in einem Spannungsfeld: Einerseits zwischen einer abolitionistischen Perspektive, welche sich gegen Strafe, Abschottung, Ausschluss (wie im herkömmlichen Rechtssystem praktiziert) und Cancelling stellt. Cancelling verhindert Auseinandersetzung mit eigenem problematischem Handeln, transformative Aufarbeitungsprozesse und ehrliche Diskurse über Vorfälle von sexualisierter Gewalt in linken Strukturen. Andererseits verstehen wir Outcalling als wichtiges Instrument, um Betroffene von sexualisierter Gewalt zu stärken, zu Sicherheit in linken Räumen beizutragen und eine konsequente Umsetzung der Definitionsmacht, sowie Schutz vor weiteren Übergriffen zu erreichen. Dabei sind wir uns bewusst, dass wir uns in einem Lernprozess befinden und wollen selbstkritisch auf unser Handeln schauen. Wir haben in vielerlei Hinsicht versagt und haben zu wenig hingeschaut oder Verantwortung übernommen.


Deshalb haben wir uns entschieden unsere Prozesse, Entwicklungen, aufgeworfene Fragen und Learnings der letzten Monate im Internet zu teilen. Wir erachten es als notwendig, über sexualisierte Gewalt zu sprechen. Auch in einer progressiven Linken sind solche Fälle leider Alltag. Es ist wichtig, dass wir hinschauen, enttabuisieren und eine Kommunikation fördern, in der wir als «Szene» sowie als Individuen wachsen können. Damit sich nachhaltig etwas ändern kann, müssen wir ein Bewusstsein für die Komplexität solcher Auseinandersetzungen erlangen.


Die Taten von Jonsi erschüttern uns schwer. Gleichzeitig wollen wir die Taten nicht als Einzelfall abtun. Wir verschliessen nicht die Augen vor der Realität: Solche Fälle haben System und sind Teil von patriarchaler Gewalt, welche wir alle mehr oder weniger mittragen und ermöglichen. Die Taten von Jonsi sind die Symptome eines tieferliegenden strukturellen Problems. Dies entschuldigt die Taten von Jonsi jedoch nicht! Denn obwohl wir die strukturellen Dimensionen begreifen wollen und ansprechen, ist uns bewusst, dass betroffene Personen auf individueller Ebene diese Taten im Jetzt aushalten und austragen müssen.


Unsere Solidarität gilt allen Betroffenen von sexualisierter Gewalt. Die Grundlage für Übergriffe jeglicher Art, gedeiht auf dem Nährboden von alltäglichem Sexismus, Verharmlosung, Tabuisierung, Täterschutz, Wegschauen, Hierachien, Macht- und Gewalt-fetisch und vielem mehr. Wie wir bei Jonsi oder auch anderen Tatpersonen sehen können, trägt eine Dazugehörigkeit zu einer «angesagten» Gruppe, Arbeitsgeber oder Wohnort (Status in der Szene, Coolness), sicherlich auch dazu bei, wie lange geschwiegen oder weggeschaut wird.


Es ist an uns hinzuschauen, Betroffenen Glauben zu schenken, «sicherere» Ort zu kreieren, an denen übergriffiges Verhalten konsequent angesprochen wird und unser Verhalten stets zu hinterfragen sowie uns selbst zu reflektieren.


Unser Prozess


Auf Wunsch einer betroffenen Person, und die Aufforderung an Jonsi sich in einem transformativen Prozess begleiten zu lassen, bildete sich im Sommer 2025 eine Bezugsgruppe. Die Bildung einer Bezugsgruppe gestaltete sich als sehr herausfordernd. Viele pflegten keine aktive Beziehung zu Jonsi, welches den Gruppenbildungsprozess stark beeinflusste: Die Arbeit blieb an wenigen Einzelpersonen hängen. Wir sind uns einer gemeinsamen Verantwortung zur Schaffung eines möglichen «Safer-spaces» in unserem Zuhause bewusst …

author: antimilitarismus
title: Украинские женщины в авангарде борьбы против бусификации – Марта Гавришко
content:
В последние дни в социальных средствах информации стремительно распространилась фотография молодой женщины из Каменского в Днепропетровской области Украины. Она стоит на коленях перед служащим ТЦК, сложив руки в мольбе. На лице написаны страх и отчаяние. Он выглядит совершенно равнодушным.

/ English / Česky / Românesc / Français / Ελληνικά / Español / Italiano / Русский / український / Magyar /

Стоящая на коленях женщина умоляет мобилизаторов не забирать ее мужа и не отправлять его на войну. Каменское, 2026 г.

Ее мольба очень проста: не забирайте моего мужа на войну!

Но военкомовец недвижим. Он должен выполнить норму, и это вступает в противоречие с ее отчаянным призывом. Армии нужны людские тела. Слезы и мольбы коленопреклоненных женщин в этот расчет не укладываются. Более того, они только создают лишние неудобства.

Сегодня эта женщина олицетворяет собой нечто большее, чем просто Украину, израненную войной, — страну, истекающую кровью и все больше отчаянно стремящуюся к прекращению насилия. Она также стала символом сопротивления принудительной мобилизации — явлению, сотрясающему Украину на пятом году полномасштабной войны, такому, которое правительство президента Владимира Зеленского уже не может легко скрыть от Запада, несмотря на тщательно культивируемые рассказы об украинской стойкости и готовности терпеть войну «столько, сколько потребуется». Женщины все чаще оказываются в авангарде этого сопротивления.

В Украине принудительная уличная мобилизация получила особое горькое жаргонное наименование: «бусификация» — так называют случаи, когда мобилизвторов обвиняют в насильственном затаскивании мужчин призывного возраста в микроавтобусы в общественных местах.

На видеороликах, распространяемых в украинских социальных сетях, можно увидеть, как женщины всех поколений вступаются, когда на мужчин нападают мобилизаторы. Они снимают на видео злоупотребления. Они публично ругают мобилизаторов за насильственные действия. Они умоляют их пощадить мужей, сыновей, братьев и незнакомцев. А когда мольбы не помогают, некоторые дают отпор — кулаками, сумками, лопатами, камнями, всем, что попадется под руку.

Другие укрывают мужчин в своих домах, магазинах и на рабочих местах, препятствуя входу сотрудников призывных служб и отказываясь выдавать тех, кто скрывается внутри.

Женщины стали лицом сопротивления бусификации.

Во-первых, женщины становятся главными очевидцами бусификации.

Улицы Украины все чаще становятся вотчиной женщин. Общественный транспорт порой напоминает пространство, разделенное по половому признаку: немногочисленные мужчины в салоне могут быть водителем, пожилым дедушкой, направляющимся на очередной прием к врачу, или беззаботным студентом, еще слишком молодым, чтобы быть призванным в армию. Все остальные — женщины.

Женщины повсюду, потому что, в отличие от мужчин призывного возраста, они могут относительно свободно передвигаться по стране — без страха быть остановленными мужчинами в форме и насильно посаженными в микроавтобус.

Большинство женщин не подлежат обязательной военной службе. Хотя в Вооруженных силах Украины служат около 75 000 украинских женщин, для большинства из них военная служба остается выбором. Для мужчин это обязанность.

Эта привилегия военного времени даёт женщинам в Украине нечто всё более ценное: свободу передвижения.

И именно поэтому женщины так часто становятся первыми свидетелями эпизодов бусификации — и первыми, кто встаёт на защиту мужчины.

Во-вторых, женщины защищают мужчин, которых любят.

Своих сыновей. Своих мужей. Своих братьев. Своих партнёров.

Они бросаются на мобилизаторов с яростью животных, защищающих своих детенышей от хищника. Матери прикрывают своих сыновей собственным телом. Жены рыдают посреди улицы, когда их мужей запихивают в фургоны, как будто их увозят на их глазах на верную смерть.

Некоторые испытывают такое отчаяние, что даже беременность не останавливает их от физического действия, чтобы предотвратить отправку своих мужей на фронт.

Другие организуются. Они собираются у территориальных призывных центров ТЦК и умоляют освободить своих мужчин. Вернее, они больше не умоляют. Они требуют.

«Мы требуем освобождения наших мужчин! Пусть отцы вернутся к своим детям. Верните сыновей к матерям, а мужей к женам. Мы требуем положить конец этим бандитским похищениям мужчин в плен».

Таков был посыл женщин, собравшихся у территориального призывного центра в Одессе, чтобы защитить своих мужей.

Женщины в Одессе пришли к ТЦК, чтобы защитить своих мужей. 2026 г.

Этот …

author: TGEU
title: TGEU at the UN Trans Advocacy Week 2026: Bringing trans voices from Albania and Kyrgyzstan to the global stage
content:
In June 2026, the UN Trans Advocacy Week (TAW) 2026 brought trans and gender diverse activists from across the world to Geneva to connect their local struggles with the international human rights system. Held alongside the 62nd session of the UN Human Rights Council (HRC62), TAW created space for activists to engage directly with UN human rights mechanisms, Member States, and civil society partners, bringing the realities and struggles of their communities directly to the United Nations. 


For activists, particularly from under-represented regions including  Eastern Europe, Central Asia and the Global South, participation in such forums would otherwise remain out of reach due to structural barriers and limited resources.


As anti-trans rhetoric grows and democratic space continues to shrink, international human rights advocacy is becoming an increasingly important tool for trans communities fighting for their rights. 


Meet the TGEU delegates


This year, TGEU, in collaboration with our partner, the

Heinrich Böll Stiftung, Tirana Office

, brought two delegates to the 62nd session of the Human Rights Council: Ariel (they/them), representing

Aleanca

 from Albania, and Kazy (them/any pronouns) from

BizdaBarbyz

, Kyrgyzstan.


Together with other trans and gender diverse activists from across the globe, Ariel and Kazy took part in discussions and advocacy on key UN reports and resolutions. This included the work of the Independent Expert on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI) and the Special Rapporteurs on health, freedom of expression, and education. 


Photo descriptions:


Left: Ariel and Kazy at TAW sessions


Middle: Ariel and Kazy with TGEU’s EECA Senior Programme Officer, Daniyar Orsekov (he/him)


Right: TAW activists with the Independent Expert on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI)


TGEU’s joint statement at the 62nd Human Rights Council (HRC62)


During HRC62, TGEU worked with partner organisations

ILGA World

 and

COC

, as well as non-binary lesbian activist Michelle Kariuki, on a joint statement delivered during the Interactive Dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression. 


The statement described a global rise in anti-trans and anti-gender movements, which use fear-based narratives to scapegoat trans and gender-diverse people while undermining human rights and democratic values. 


It also highlighted the growing role of digital platforms in these attacks, arguing that failing to address harmful online environments can threaten freedom of expression and civic participation while enabling broader anti-rights and authoritarian agendas.


Video description: Michelle Kariuki, delivering the joint statement during the Interactive Dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression


TAW side event: Defending freedom of association 


TAW partners also organised a dedicated side event during HRC62: Democratic backsliding through attacks on freedoms of expression, association and assembly. The event brought together activists and advocates to discuss the shrinking space for trans, LGBTI, and feminist movements, share strategies for resisting democratic erosion, and reflect on the future of engagement with global human rights mechanisms. 


TGEU’s EECA Senior Programme Officer, Daniyar Orsekov (he/him), delivered an intervention at the event addressing the growing restrictions on freedom of association faced by trans and LGBTI organisations across Europe and Central Asia: 


“Protecting freedom of association is not only about safeguarding one particular community. It is about protecting democracy itself and preserving society’s ability to organise, defend its rights, and resist authoritarianism.”


read the statement


In conclusion


International spaces such as the United Nations are most meaningful when they are connected to the realities of communities on the ground. TAW 2026 brought activists together to share experiences, build solidarity and strengthen collective advocacy at a time when trans and wider civil society movements are facing growing pressure. For TGEU, supporting activists from our region to participate in these spaces helps ensure their experiences and expertise shape international human rights discussions. 


The work does not end in Geneva: the relationships built, skills learnt, and experiences shared during Trans …

author: Lauren Rankin
title: The Win for Abortion Rights in Indiana Has Reshaped the National Legal Landscape
content:
The ruling sets the stage for further free speech protections for those who help abortion seekers who cross state lines.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The national legal landscape has become just a little bit brighter for those who have been working tirelessly to help abortion seekers in Republican-controlled areas cross state lines to access abortion care.

Reproductive rights advocates nationwide are hopeful that last week’s decision about an Indiana law by the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals could potentially have wide-reaching implications for nationwide efforts to protect patients’ right to access abortion information and enable more health care providers to continue assisting abortion seekers.

In a significant win for abortion rights in the post-Roe U.S., on August 18 the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals struck down an Indiana law that barred abortion providers from helping minors find abortions outside of the state or even sharing information about abortion. This ruling has nationwide implications because it could lead to further free speech protections for those who share abortion information and support travel for abortion seekers.

It has been three years since Indiana’s total abortion ban took effect, outlawing nearly every abortion in the state. For three years, reproductive health providers have been forced to turn away abortion seekers, their hands tied by the state’s draconian ban.

However, reproductive health providers in Indiana, like Planned Parenthood, didn’t just turn people away without support — they did their best to help abortion seekers figure out where they could get an abortion. Abortion is legal in surrounding states, including Michigan, Ohio, and Illinois, the latter of which has fast become a hub for abortion seekers from across the country. After Indiana’s total abortion took effect, the state’s Planned Parenthood continued to provide information about abortion care to abortion seekers, including minors; helped them find a clinic in a neighboring state; and helped minors book an appointment.

That didn’t sit well with Indiana abortion opponents, who argued that sharing information about abortion with minors is illegal. In 2017, Indiana enacted an “aid-or-assist” law, which bans helping a minor access an abortion without explicit parental consent. That law, coupled with the state’s total abortion ban, emboldened abortion opponents to keep reproductive health care providers from sharing information with or even helping a minor find a clinic outside of the state. Even discussing abortion with a minor should be considered a violation of that law, Indiana’s Attorney General Todd Rokita argued in court filings.

Not so, said the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals in Planned Parenthood v. Commissioner of the Indiana State Department of Health. In a stinging rebuke of hardliners’ desperate attempt to crush anyone seeking a safe, legal abortion anywhere, the court upheld a permanent injunction against the “aid-or-assist” law. A minor has the right to access information about abortion services from reproductive health care providers without parental consent, the court ruled. The “aid-or-assist” law would constitute a content-based restriction on protected speech and is therefore unconstitutional.

The Seventh Circuit has ruled that states cannot keep their citizens, including minors, from learning about or seeking abortion services outside the state.

This ruling has wide-reaching implications, as states with abortion bans have tried new and increasingly draconian means of stopping any information or access to abortion services for their own citizens.

While a state can ban abortion, per the Dobbs ruling, the Seventh Circuit has ruled that states cannot keep their citizens, including minors, from learning about or seeking abortion services outside the state. The fundamental right to share and consume information (a.k.a. freedom of speech) cannot be infringed upon just because some far right lawmakers don’t like that kind of speech. Helping someone to obtain an abortion outside of a banned state, and talking about abortion, including to those under the age of 18, are both protected by the Constitution.

Abortion opponents in Indiana can choose to appeal this case to the Supreme Court. But if they do, the Seventh Circuit might have created its own safety valve to preserve this opinion. As Madiba K. Dennie …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Igualdad de género? : Por qué el reclutamiento de las mujeres en Ucrania se ha vuelto inevitable
content:
En la página web del gobierno ucraniano aparecieron dos peticiones que solicitan la extensión del servicio militar obligatorio a las mujeres. Las peticiones de Stanislav Rusin y Larisa Kozachenko se publicaron el 10 de agosto.Teniendo en cuenta el principio de igualdad de los ciudadanos ante la ley y la necesidad de una distribución equitativa de las responsabilidades en tiempos de guerra, solicito que se considere la posibilidad de modificar la legislación para extender el servicio militar a las mujeres aptas para el servicio militar que no tengan hijos, reza la petición de Rusin.


La propuesta de Kozachenko resultó ser más radical, exigiendo que prácticamente todas las mujeres que cumplan los requisitos de edad, salud y otros criterios sean enviadas al frente.


La cuestión del posible reclutamiento de mujeres recuerda mucho a un tema igualmente impopular que se debatió en 2023, cuando Ucrania aprobó una enmienda a la ley de reclutamiento que reducía la edad mínima para el servicio militar obligatorio. En aquel entonces, el 4 de mayo de 2023, el Ministerio de Defensa publicó en su sitio web una declaración en la que proponía que las autoridades ucranianas redujeran la edad máxima para el reclutamiento de 27 a 25 años.


Al día siguiente, el 5 de mayo de 2023, el Consejo de Ministros aprobó un proyecto de ley para reducir la edad de reclutamiento de 27 a 25 años. Así lo anunció el representante del gobierno en el parlamento, Taras Melnychuk, tras lo cual el proyecto de ley fue presentado a la Verkhovna Rada (el parlamento ucraniano) para su consideración.


El 30 de mayo de 2023, en menos de un mes, Ucrania redujo la edad de reclutamiento militar obligatorio de 27 a 25 años; el proyecto de ley correspondiente, el n.º 9281, contó con el apoyo de 304 diputados. Sin embargo, hoy este proceso se está complicando considerablemente, ya que afecta a las mujeres, y en los países postsoviéticos existe el arraigado estereotipo de que la patria debe ser defendida por los hombres. Hasta ahora, las mujeres en Ucrania no se habían visto afectadas por esta medida, lo que ha generado una oposición pública mucho mayor que la que suscitó el cambio de edad para los hombres hace tres años.


Tres días después de la publicación de la petición, el 13 de agosto de 2026, el diputado de la Rada Suprema, Dmytro Razumkov, criticó abiertamente las iniciativas del gobierno. «Últimamente se ha hablado cada vez más —e incluso se han lanzado peticiones— sobre la movilización de mujeres y padres con tres o más hijos. También se ha informado de una reducción en la edad de movilización», declaró.


Además, comentaristas de los medios ucranianos se sumaron al debate. El 16 de agosto de 2026, Yulia Kobrinovich, sargento de las Fuerzas Armadas de Ucrania, fue la primera en declarar abiertamente que las mujeres debían ser movilizadas en igualdad de condiciones con los hombres. «Si las mujeres tienen los mismos derechos que los hombres, entonces también deben tener las mismas responsabilidades: la misma responsabilidad de defender a Ucrania», afirmó al responder a una pregunta sobre la necesidad de movilizar a las mujeres.


La semana siguiente, el 17 de agosto de 2026, Volodymyr Zelensky presentó un proyecto de ley ante la Rada Suprema proponiendo ampliar oficialmente las fuentes de reclutamiento para las Fuerzas Armadas de Ucrania, pero de forma discreta y sin publicidad. Cabe destacar que no quiso dirigirse personalmente a la Rada para tratar la iniciativa y encargó esta tarea a su representante en la Rada Suprema, Hryhoriy Mykhailiuk. Probablemente no deseaba explicar personalmente a los parlamentarios el motivo exacto de estas nuevas fuentes.


Sin embargo, tan pronto como el proyecto de ley se hizo público y comenzaron los debates, fue retirado inmediatamente del sitio web de la Rada Suprema. Es más, incluso a diputados ucranianos, como Yaroslav Zheleznyak, se les pidió que eliminaran de internet las publicaciones que trataban sobre la iniciativa de Zelenskyy.


Conscientes del profundo descontento público ante la posibilidad de reclutar mujeres, las autoridades ucranianas han seguido forzando los límites de la ventana de Overton. «Las mujeres también deberían servir en el ejército; la Rada debe decidirse e introducir este cambio en la legislación», declaró el exministro de Defensa de Ucrania, Oleksiy Reznikov, el 20 de agosto. «Algunos puestos en la retaguardia podrían ser ocupados por mujeres, lo que permitiría desplegar a más hombres más cerca …

content:
RDV

 le 30/08/2026 à partir de 17h à La Mutinerie (176 rue Saint-Martin, 75003 Paris) pour la pré-rentrée de Queer Education.


Blindtest et petits jeux pour bien commencer l'année scolaire

 

!

author: anred
title: Once años de organización y lucha: llega el 11.º Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur
content:
El próximo 5 de septiembre, mujeres, lesbianas, travestis, trans, intersex, bisexuales y personas no binaries del conurbano sur se reunirán en Monte Grande para compartir experiencias, debatir las problemáticas de los territorios y fortalecer las redes de organización colectiva. La jornada tendrá talleres, feria autogestiva, caravana, rondas de debate y espacios de participación accesibles e inclusivos.

Por ANRed 


El próximo 5 de septiembre se realizará en Monte Grande el 11.º Encuentro Regional de Mujeres, Lesbianas, Travestis, Trans, Intersex, Bisexuales y No Binaries de Zona Sur, una nueva jornada de encuentro, organización y construcción colectiva que reunirá a quienes vienen sosteniendo redes y experiencias de lucha en los territorios del conurbano sur.


A once años de su primera edición, el encuentro vuelve a plantearse como un espacio para poner en común las problemáticas que atraviesan a los distintos territorios, compartir saberes y experiencias y construir herramientas colectivas frente a las desigualdades y las violencias. La propuesta recupera la memoria de los encuentros anteriores y busca, al mismo tiempo, fortalecer las redes comunitarias y proyectar nuevas formas de participación y organización.


“Como desde hace once años estamos aquí organizades para debatir, intercambiar pero sobretodo reafirmar nuestra lucha en este contexto adverso, crisis económica y ataque a nuestro transfeminismo que ha logrado cambios en la sociedad en estos últimos años. Les esperamos a todes quienes quieran participar de esta experiencia enriquecedora”, expresó una de las organizadoras.


Una jornada para encontrarse y organizarse


La jornada comenzará a las 10:30 en la Plaza de las Artes, donde será el punto de encuentro. A las 11:30 se realizará la apertura formal y comenzarán los talleres de autodefensa, primeros auxilios y violencia digital —Ley EMA—. Luego, a las 12:30, habrá una feria autogestiva para compartir producciones y seguir fortaleciendo los vínculos entre quienes participan.


A las 13:30 se realizará una caravana hacia el Instituto 35, donde continuarán las actividades con las rondas de debate. Desde las 14, los espacios de discusión abordarán distintas dimensiones de la vida cotidiana y las luchas territoriales: salud, cuidados y derecho a decidir; trabajo, precarización y derechos laborales; educación pública, acceso y organización; violencias, prevención y acompañamiento; y derechos humanos, memoria y defensa de las conquistas alcanzadas.


El cierre será a las 16, con una instancia de conclusiones destinada a recuperar lo trabajado durante la jornada y pensar colectivamente los próximos pasos.


Accesibilidad y participación


Uno de los ejes destacados de esta edición será la accesibilidad. El encuentro contará con un equipo de Lengua de Señas Argentina (LSA) para favorecer la participación de personas sordas y dispondrá también de un espacio de calma sensorial, pensado para quienes necesiten transitar la jornada con menor estímulo.


Desde la organización remarcan que la participación de todas las personas es fundamental para construir un encuentro verdaderamente inclusivo y proponen continuar derribando las barreras capacitistas que atraviesan los espacios y territorios.


En un contexto atravesado por la crisis económica y por disputas en torno a derechos y conquistas construidas durante años de organización, el encuentro se propone como un espacio para volver a encontrarse, intercambiar experiencias y reafirmar que la organización colectiva sigue siendo una herramienta fundamental.

author: Kelly Cvetkova
title: Why One Nation is attacking women
content:
Pauline Hanson has spat in the faces of the millions of Australian women who have experienced family violence by describing the crime as a “two-way street”. Returning to a tired victim-blaming rhetoric that women just “shouldn’t put up with it”, she’s trying to turn the clock back on attitudes to women experiencing violence and the real difficulties they face getting support. 

Hanson has featured on right-wing podcasts asserting that women are treating the family courts and child support payments as a “cash cow”, a system that needs to be “reined in”. These comments not only fly in the face of reality but are also an attack on some of the poorest and most vulnerable people in Australia. The 2025 Household, Income and Labour Dynamics survey found that 34.7 percent of children in single parent households live in poverty. Eight out of every ten of these households are headed by women. Domestic abuse is the main reason women become homeless in Australia, women and children making up nine out of the ten people attempting to access specialist housing services. 

Hanson’s outbursts are not the result of ignorance. One Nation’s increased attacks against the rights of women, whether on the issues of domestic abuse, abortion rights or parental leave, are part of the intensification of its far-right agenda, and an attempt to integrate a broader range of social issues into it. Women, according to this logic, are just another interest group that gets “special treatment” thanks to wokeism and whose endless demands are a drain on business and wealth creation. In her now infamous speech at the National Press Club, Hanson made this clear, stating “if women take time off [to have children] and they are not paid their wages because they’re not working, fair enough ... Why should business pay? They’re not at work”.

This parallels her attacks on organisations like the National Indigenous Australians Agency, which she argues should be abolished to save taxpayers from “wasteful Indigenous grants”. She likewise attacks LGBTI people, specifically the “transgender insurgency”, that has “penetrated almost every regulatory authority”. Who is on the other side of this equation?  Apparently, as Hanson told parliament in 2023, “the most oppressed and neglected minority in Australia”, is—wait for it—“men”. 

The positioning around women’s rights is also intended to garner One Nation stronger support with a wider and more hardcore base of potential members and campaigners, most recently on the issue of abortion.

While the party has always maintained sexist talking points about the family courts and the evils of feminism, it has not previously actively campaigned against abortion rights. Hanson has been testing the waters on this issue lately though, indicating that she thinks Australia needs to “have a conversation” about abortion and flagging that she thinks abortion rights should be restricted after twenty weeks. She’s rubbed shoulders with the likes of infamous anti-abortion activist and influencer Joanna Howe. When Malcolm Roberts was questioned at a Brisbane Christian conference about whether the party would move to a policy of banning abortion altogether, the One Nation senator said that it was “becoming [his] goal” to do so.

Barnaby Joyce has been the most explicit in why the change of approach has come now. Speaking to a Sydney crowd of anti-abortion demonstrators, he stated, “What I see before me here is about 1,500 people who can hand out how to vote cards”. One Nation has a clear desire to recruit those sections of the right who are motivated by this issue. And why not—they are an already organised layer of activists who can be relatively easily deployed to campaign, especially if One Nation seems able to deliver and potentially reverse their flagging fortunes. 

Abortion has, in practice, been a settled issue in Australian politics for decades. Nearly three in every four people support legal abortion in some or all cases. But the right know both that there is a motivated minority available to them, and are confident that an aggressive campaign can swing more people behind the cause—especially when Labor is too cowardly to fight on the issue, as it was during the Voice referendum, for example. And the reality is that attitudes to abortion are already going backwards. A

Guardian

 Essential poll found that between November 2024 and July 2026, the percentage of people who agree abortion should be legal in all cases dropped from 41 to …

title: A propos du régime autocratique du président Kais Saïed et de la montée du racisme en Tunisie
content:
Ce document veut analyser l'ascension du populisme et du racisme utilisés par Kaïs Saïed et parmi la population en Tunisie. Déjà, avant et pendant son accession aux rennes de l'État, le président en Tunisie, s'était rendu populaire en se présentant d'abord comme proche des travailleurs et de la population, et en ayant fait de l'anti-élite et la lutte contre la corruption son principal, voire son unique, axe politique.


Pour rappel, la population tunisienne avait déjà dans son histoire mené un soulèvement, à savoir la révolution du jasmin du 17 Décembre 2010 au 14 Janvier 2011 qui a culminé sur la fin du règne de feu le dictateur Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali, donc au règne d'un tyran. Déjà cela. Mais cette révolte s'était arrêtée par son déraillement avec la mise en place d'un gouvernement transitoire qui, en pratique, a dépossédé les travailleurs et la population de leur destin et donc finalement de leurs capacités de prendre des décisions politiques.


Une grande partie des travailleurs en Tunisie s'étaient régulièrement mobilisés contre tous les nouveaux gouvernements «

 

post révolution

 

» de «

 

l'après Ben Ali

 

» qui ont suivi, sachant qu'ils n'avaient promis que faux espoirs et chimères. C'était alors dans ce contexte-là que Kaïs Saïed avait saisi l'opportunité de se mettre en avant (avec la complicité d'une partie de la bourgeoisie) pour se présenter comme le champion de la logique anti système et contre la corruption puis d'accroître progressivement sa popularité et son influence.


Avec ce populisme, Kaïs Saïed est rapidement devenu, au début et en l'espace d'une dizaine d'années, une figure de «

 

sauveur du peuple

 

» tunisien. Et cette image s'est consolidée lorsqu'il a remporté l'élection présidentielle tunisienne de 2019 avec une large victoire en se présentant comme un candidat anti-élite, proche des travailleurs et du peuple, extérieur aux partis traditionnels, islamistes, démocrates, etc…ainsi qu'étranger aux magouilles.


Mais progressivement, sa politique devint de plus en plus autoritaire. Et pour cause, en 2021, il a suspendu le Parlement et concentré ses pouvoirs pour imposer en 2022 une nouvelle constitution lui confirmant les pleins pouvoirs.


À partir de là, ce seront plusieurs opposants qui seront arrêtés. En 2023, plusieurs figures de l'opposition de tout bord politique ont été arrêtées et jugées dans des affaires dites de «

 

complot contre la sûreté de l'État

 

» et via leur procès en 2025, certains ont même été condamnés à de très lourdes peines, allant jusqu'à plus de 20 ans de prison, ce qui est du jamais vu depuis la chute de feu le tyran Ben Ali.


L'organisation et la contestation par les travailleurs en Tunisie devant ces mesures autoritaires commencent alors à monter. Et sachant que son pouvoir était susceptible de vaciller tôt ou tard, ce président Kaïs Saïed a alors lancé (d'ailleurs également sur recommandation de certains de ses parrains de l'Occident) une politique démagogique raciste et anti-immigration visant les migrants africains Subsahariens. Et avec le support de la bourgeoisie nationale, cette politique cherche à la fois à diviser les travailleurs et la population et à détourner la colère des classes populaires vers une haine raciste pour casser le potentiel de contestation, mettre au pas la population pour qu'elle ne bronche pas, étant focalisée sur le faux problème de l'immigration subsaharienne, et ainsi aider à renforcer davantage l'image respectable de ce pouvoir brutal. Ainsi, en plus des expulsions, cette politique raciste s'est accompagnée de vagues d'arrestations policières, de mise en examens et d'emprisonnement de militants ou de personnalités antiracistes et outre les expulsions, d'abandons dans le désert, ce qui est criminel

 

! C'est inhumain, en plus d'être destiné à mettre au pas la population, d'autant plus que ces migrants sont des personnes qui passent par la Tunisie de manière temporaire dans l'espoir de rejoindre l'Europe pour espérer (d'ailleurs très souvent sans succès) une vie meilleure suite aux dégâts causés dans leurs pays à cause des dictatures placées par les grandes puissances si ce n'est pas par ces dernières elles-mêmes.


Cette montée du racisme dans la culture et la mentalité «

 

populaire

 

» est la suite logique de cette politique gouvernementale populiste. C'est également lié au nationalisme et au patriotisme, tous les deux forts en Tunisie, car en parlant en terme de «

 

peuple

 

» et en réduisant tout à …
