author: Danilo Arao
title: Kapamilya
content:
At least 5,000 workers have been retrenched since the shutdown (Photo by Carlo Manalansan / Bulatlat)

Sa ngayon, tahimik ang mga lansangan. Pero hindi permanente ang pananahimik.

Posibleng huling pagbisita. Pero sana’y maulit pa hangga’t hindi pa huli ang lahat.

Sa halip na phone patch o Zoom interview na madalas na nangyayari, naisipan nilang gawin ang panayam sa mismong studio ng ABS-CBN. Nangangahulugan itong muling pagbisita sa gusaling medyo kabisado na dahil wala namang masyadong nagbago sa mga nakaraang dekada.

Alam pa rin ang mesa o estasyon ng mga kakilala’t kaibigan, lalo na ang mga dating estudyante sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas (UP). Wala pa ring nagbago sa lokasyon ng mga kubeta kaya alam ang pupuntahan kung kailangang tugunan ang tawag ng kalikasan.

Siyempre’y likas pa rin ang ngiti’t pagbati, lalo na sa mga saksi sa nangyari noong 2020. Sa mga medyo bata pang staff at reporter, may mga nakipagkamay at nagpakilala. Ganyan talaga ang mga may alam sa kasaysayan at kolektibong paninindigan.

Halata ang saya sa pagkikita pero iba ang pahiwatig ng mga mata. Tila may gustong sabihin pero huwag muna. Tulad ng ibang newsroom, abala kasi ang lahat sa pagbabalita ng nagmamadaling kasaysayan.

Pero halata namang may kakaiba sa ABS-CBN newsroom sa kasalukuyan dahil sa hindi katanggap-tanggap na nakaraan. Anim na taon ang nakalipas mula nang ipagkait ng mga nasa kapangyarihan ang broadcast franchise nito. Tuwang-tuwa ang mga bulag na tagasuporta ng nakaraang administrasyon. Sa loob-loob nila, “Sa wakas, napatahimik ang kritiko!”

Pero nanahimik nga ba? Kung ano ang ingay para ipaglaban ang kalayaan sa pamamahayag, mas tumindi pa mula nang marinig ang mga baluktot na depensa ng maraming personaheng may kakabit na “His Excellency” o “Honorable” sa pangalan.

Sabi nila, walang kinalaman sa kalayaan sa pamamahayag ang pagpapasara dahil simpleng paglabag lang ito sa regulasyon tungkol sa prangkisa. Pero ilang beses nang napabulaanan ang mga walang batayang akusasyon tulad ng diumanong hindi pagbabayad ng buwis, dayuhang pagmamay-ari at pagpapakalat ng pekeng balita.

Dahil isinapubliko ang pagdinig sa Kamara de Representantes noong 2020, saksi ang buong Pilipinas sa sinabi ng isang mambabatas na nagagalit siya sa ABS-CBN dahil hindi iniulat ang pamimigay niya ng bigas. Ito rin ang mambabatas na binanggit ngayong taon lang na bayaran daw ang karamihan sa midya. Kahit na nakakulong siya sa kasalukuyan dahil sa isang non-bailable na kaso, wala pa ring hustisya dahil wala pang napapanagot sa naging maling desisyon ng Kongreso tungkol sa ABS-CBN.

Hahayaan na lang ba ang nangyari? Tama bang “Move on!” ang maging perspektiba dahil sinabi ng pamunuan ng ABS-CBN na hindi na kasama sa kanilang estratehiya ang aplikasyon para sa bagong prangkisa? Nararapat bang tumahimik na lang dahil naibenta na ang mga ari-arian, partikular ang lupang kinatitirikan ng gusali?

Batay sa impormasyong isinapubliko, ang tatlong ektaryang lupain ng ABS-CBN ay nasa kamay na ng Ayala Land, Inc. Magtatayo raw ng “mixed use commercial and residential development.” Posibleng magkakaron ng condominium units, office rental spaces, commercial centers at kahit na shopping malls kung pagbabatayan ang mga proyekto nito sa Cloverleaf, Arca South at Makati Central Business District.

Ano kaya ang plano sa ABS-CBN Main Broadcast Building, Dolphy Theater at ang Millennium Transmitter? Tuluyan bang gigibain ang mga ito sa kabila ng halaga nito sa kasaysayan ng midya sa Pilipinas?

Bilang paghahanda sa demolisyon, nakasara na ang Sgt. Esguerra main gate na ilang beses na pinasok at pinaradahan. Kaya sa pagpasok muli sa gusali, kailangang dumaan sa side entrance. Nakaparada pa rin ang maraming sasakyan ng ABS-CBN pero halatang marurumi na ang iba dahil hindi na masyadong nagagamit.

Sa loob ng gusali, may mga nagtatrabaho pa rin pero may ilang lugar na halos wala nang tao. Halatang medyo napapabayaan na ang ilang bahagi dahil hindi na masyadong nalilinis. Ang studio na pinagdausan ng taping, malinis naman pero halatang make-shift na lang at hindi permanente. Kung sabagay, nalalapit na ang paglipat para magbigay-daan sa mga bagong may-ari.

Pagkatapos ng taping at habang hinihintay ang sasakyang maghahatid pabalik sa kampus, pansamantalang nakausap ang isang taga-ABS-CBN. Maraming off-the-record na napagkuwentuhan. Halata ang lungkot sa nangyari noong 2020. Nang mapag-usapan ang isang nakakulong na mambabatas, pinagkuwentuhan ang “karma” sa kabila ng patuloy na …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Not one surfaced despite court orders, families demand review of legal remedies
content:
Families of desaparecidos (enforced disappearance victims) and human rights defenders protest in front of the Supreme Court (SC) to push for the immediate review of writs of amparo and habeas data on August 28, 2026, on the eve of International Day of the Disappeared. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

“Not a single success story, not one was recovered even with orders from the court.”

MANILA — Left with no choice but to push back, families of enforced disappearance victims called on the Supreme Court to review the writs of amparo and habeas data for “persistent ineffectiveness” for nearly two decades.

“Not a single success story, not one was recovered even with orders from the court,” Edith Burgos, mother of disappeared activist Jonas Burgos, told Bulatlat in an interview. She is the president of International Coalition Against Enforced Disappearance (ICAED) and vice chairperson of human rights group Karapatan.

Read: Bulatlat’s special archives on Jonas Burgos

The writ of amparo, which took effect in 2007, is supposed to protect an individual’s rights to life, liberty, and security against unlawful threats or violations. The writ of habeas data which took effect in 2008 is supposed to provide a remedy against unlawful gathering, collection, or storage of personal information and protects a person’s right to privacy.

“We wrote to the Chief Justice because there have been no positive results. We listed all the cases here and it is high time for the Supreme Court to review their own administrative order for the writs,” Cora Jazmines, wife of disappeared labor activist James Jazmines and one of the signatories of the letter sent to the SC, said in Filipino.

Read: A year after husband’s disappearance, Corazon finds more questions than answers

Since the writs took effect, human rights group Karapatan and Desaparecidos documented 272 cases of enforced disappearance: 206 cases in the administration of Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, 29 cases during Benigno Aquino III, 20 cases during Rodrigo Duterte’s administration, and Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has 17 cases as of this writing.

Prior to Arroyo’s administration, there were at least 2,000 unresolved cases of enforced disappearances.

“Rather than ensuring immediate protection and accountability, many petitions have been met with procedural delays, dismissals, or orders that are inadequately enforced. The persistence of disappearances across successive administrations—and the continued rise in cases even after the writ’s promulgation— exposes systemic failures in the implementation and enforcement of human rights protections,” Desaparecidos, a group of families and friends of victims, said in their letter.

Below are the following cases that the groups cited:

Karen Empeño, Sherlyn Cadapan, and Manuel Merino (Disappeared June 26, 2006, Hagonoy, Bulacan): The writ of amparo was filed on October 24, 2007, with the Supreme Court issuing the writ on October 25, 2007. Despite the Court of Appeals ordering their immediate release on September 17, 2008, the victims remain missing.

Romulas Robiños (Disappeared November 17, 2006, City of San Fernando, Pampanga): The Supreme Court issued a writ of amparo on November 8, 2007, but the Court of Appeals later dismissed the petition citing “lack of evidence.” He remains missing.

Nilo Arado and Maria Luisa Posa-Dominado (Disappeared April 12, 2007, Oton, Iloilo): A writ of amparo was granted by the Iloilo Regional Trial Court on December 17, 2007, ordering their release. They remain missing.

Jonas Burgos (Disappeared April 28, 2007, Quezon City): The writ of amparo was issued by the Supreme Court on December 24, 2007. The Court of Appeals partially granted the writ on July 17, 2008, ordering investigations. He remains missing.

James Balao (Disappeared September 17, 2008, La Trinidad, Benguet): The writ of amparo was partly issued on October 9, 2008, but later reversed on January 19, 2009. He remains missing.

Elizabeth “Loi” Magbanua (Disappeared May 3, 2022, Valenzuela City, Metro Manila): The Supreme Court issued the writ of amparo on August 23, 2022, and the Court of Appeals held the military accountable on September 9, 2022. Magbanua remains missing.

Maria Elena Pampoza and Elgene Mungcal (Disappeared July 3, 2022, Moncada, Tarlac): The writ of amparo was granted by the Supreme Court on November 29, 2022. They remain missing.

William Lariosa (Disappeared April 10, 2024, Quezon, Bukidnon): After dismissal of habeas corpus and amparo …

author: Unknown
title: Gülistan Doku investigation: 10 people taken into custody
content:
A fifth wave of operations was carried out as part of the investigation into the disappearance of Gülistan Doku in Dêrsim. Ten people were detained as part of the investigation. New findings have been uncovered, including new PTS and communication records, suspicious access to and activity on Gülistan Doku’s Instagram account, and new evidence concerning underwater searches.


It was reported that records in a diver’s logbook, which had been determined to have been concealed from judicial authorities, did not match the official search reports. It was also stated that evidence had been obtained suggesting that some of Gülistan Doku’s personal belongings may have been placed underwater at a later stage in order to create the appearance of evidence supporting the possibility of suicide.

title: Veysi Aktaş: Our resistance must be as great as the dreams of the martyrs
content:
As a condolence gathering held for the Kurdistan Freedom Martyrs in the Cizîra Botan district of Şirnex came to an end on its third day, a commemoration was held under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture of Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER).


Thousands of people from Cizre Botan and surrounding provinces and districts attended the commemoration, held in front of the DEM Party’s Cizre district office, along with families of the martyrs and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.


Entering the commemoration area to slogans of “Long Live Leader Apo” and “Martyrs are Immortal,” accompanied by ululations, people placed photographs of Leader Apo and the martyrs on the platform. The platform also displayed Leader Apo’s words: “My martyred comrades and I worked along the path of love. Those who remain must know how to walk this path.”


Photographs of Mahsum Korkmaz (Egîd), one of the PKK’s first commanders, and Zeynep Kınacı (Zîlan) were also displayed, alongside a large photograph of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan].


The program began with a moment of silence, followed by the singing of the “Çarxa Şoreşê” anthem.


“We will never forget them”


Speaking at the commemoration, MEBYA-DER executive Esmer Çıkmaz said that, as the families of martyrs, they would continue the struggle for peace and freedom.


Esmer Çıkmaz said, “As mothers, we made them a promise: We will bring peace and freedom to this country. We will never forget them. We will bring peace and freedom to this country.”


“To honor the martyrs is to uphold their goal”


DEM Party Mêrdîn MP Beritan Güneş Altın noted that people from different parts of Kurdistan had attended the commemoration and paid tribute to the martyrs.


Stating that honoring the martyrs means upholding their goals, Beritan Güneş Altın said: “To honor the martyrs means to uphold their goals, to create a democratic society. To honor the martyrs means to uphold Leader Apo’s paradigm and to uphold peace.”


Beritan Güneş Altın said that Öcalan’s physical freedom must be secured, adding, “Those who ask what the Kurdish people want should look at this photograph. The Kurdish people want peace despite their pain; they want to live together.”


Veysi Aktaş, a member of the Imralı Secretariat, said that Cizre Botan is the land of the story of Mem û Zîn, describing the martyrs as the contemporary representatives of that story.


Aktaş said: “Every male comrade who has fallen as a martyr is Mem. Every female comrade who has fallen as a martyr is Zîn. Because, just like Mem, they gave their lives for freedom.”


Saying that the martyrs fought for a free future, Aktaş stated, “Each of our martyrs is a hero who completes the unfinished story of Mem and Zîn with a free future.”


“Our resistance must be as great as their dreams”


Aktaş said that the martyrs were not merely fighters, but people who struggled to build a democratic and equal society, adding: “Every woman and man who fell as a martyr waged this resistance not only for themselves, but to liberate an entire society.


Our resistance must be as great as their dreams; their spirit is a source of strength and inspiration for us.”


“Everyone should take their place in democratic politics”


Referring to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Aktaş said that the people must participate in the process and called for participation in democratic politics. He added: “That is why we are beginning a new struggle. We are beginning democratic politics. Let everyone take their place here. Our destiny depends on us.”

author: Unknown
title: Doğan: Öcalan must have the conditions to fulfil his historic role
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan held a press conference at the party’s headquarters on the Central Executive Board meeting held on Thursday, 27 August, and current developments.


Ayşegül Doğan said: “The framework law, developments in Syria, the resistance of Doruk Mining workers, the condolence gatherings held recently and missing-person notices were discussed extensively. Of course, another important issue was the congress we will hold on 6 September.”


Framework law: Coordinated work


Ayşegül Doğan began her remarks with the framework law and continued: “The Monitoring and Evaluation Board, which will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the process under the law, has been established. The Monitoring and Evaluation Board held its first meeting on 24 August. Our Central Executive Board considers the fact that it held its first meeting and began its work to be a highly significant development. To coordinate the work, a total of four bodies have been established: the Judicial and Legal Affairs Board, the Monitoring and Assessment Board, the Social Cohesion and Integration Subcommittee, and the Disarmament and Strategy Coordination Subcommittee. One of our greatest expectations is that these bodies will work inclusively and in coordination with one another, in keeping with the pace of the historic process we are going through. We believe that, in the coming period, it will become clearer how these bodies will work, who will serve on them, and how they will coordinate and work in concert with one another.”


Mechanisms that include different sections of society


Doğan said: “Even before these boards began to be established, we had been saying the same thing from the very first day of the process: this cannot be confined solely to a bureaucratic mechanism. We are talking about a demand for peace and democracy, and about making that demand a reality. There is an immense and considerable effort in Turkey in this regard. That effort must also feed into these boards, and this contribution must be reflected in their work. What do I mean by this? We need to create opportunities for civil society to contribute and for people with experience in this field to bring the knowledge they have accumulated over the years into these boards, while also enabling them to follow the process. In other words, it would be beneficial to effectively put in place mechanisms that can include different sections of society in these boards. As always, this was one of the critical points we discussed within our Central Executive Board. We call this the Peace and Democratic Society Process. We are talking about a process of building something new, and we have all experienced and seen how critical it is for society’s support to be directly visible in this process.”


Conditions for Abdullah Öcalan


Doğan also said: “Another expectation of ours, and another critical issue, is that Mr. Öcalan must be provided with the opportunities and conditions necessary to carry out the weighty and historic responsibility he has assumed in this process. As you know, this is not something we are saying for the first time. Every stage we have gone through so far has shown us why he needs to take part in this process effectively, with conditions that allow for uninterrupted communication. This is not only a matter of coordinating disarmament. To put it in Mr. Öcalan’s own words, another point that is highly critical for our party is that his position in this process must be clearly defined and that he must be placed in a position where he can provide coordination in order to make the historic Kurdish-Turkish alliance and coexistence permanent. Mr. Öcalan also says, ‘Let us build a shared life together, with the awareness that patiently opening this path is a historic opportunity, and by abandoning simplistic, narrow approaches that do not serve the future.’ We strongly underline these words. In doing so, we also want to offer a reminder about language. The language of this new period must also be shaped by new expressions and new words. Instead of language that constantly accuses, questions and judges, we must be able to develop a language through which we can empathise with one another, while taking mutual sensitivities into consideration. This is another issue to which our party attaches great importance.”

title: Karayılan: Our martyrs sacrificed themselves for the success of our people
content:
Murat Karayılan, a member of the People’s Defense Center (HSM) Command, answered ANF’s questions and spoke about the recently announced deaths of guerrilla fighters, the commemorations and condolence gatherings held in many cities across Kurdistan, the reasons for the delay in announcing the deaths, the status of the remains, and solidarity with the families of those who lost their lives. 


Part one of this interview can be read

here

. 


What can you say about the families’ requests to recover the remains of the martyr guerrillas? Of course, deaths are a reality of war in a struggle for freedom that has lasted for more than 50 years. Yet the remains of very few guerrillas are handed over to their families. The whereabouts of many of the martyrs are not even known. Families are making strong and persistent demands to recover the remains of their loved ones. What can you say about this?


This is also an important issue for us. As is known, from the Republican era to the present day, because they sought to annihilate our society, Kurdish society, they wanted the heroes to be forgotten and not commemorated; they aimed to erase our memory. In other words, they wanted us to lose our history. For this reason, from the very beginning until today, the locations of the graves of those who lost their lives in the Kurdish uprisings have remained unknown. The burial places of Sheikh Said, Seyit Rıza, those who lost their lives in Geliyê Zilan and those who fell in the Ağrı Resistance remain unknown. Until the 1990s, our martyr comrades were also largely denied the right to be commemorated. For example, the whereabouts of the remains of comrade Egîd (Mahsum Korkmaz) are still unknown. The graves of all the comrades from that period remain unknown. This largely remained the case until 2000. As is known, there was a ceasefire between 2013 and 2015. During that period, we established many cemeteries for our martyr comrades in Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) and Southern Kurdistan (Başur), and brought our martyr comrades together there.


When the war resumed, our cemeteries were also targeted. This is well known; the public knows it, everyone knows it. In Garzan, they even exhumed the bones of our martyr comrades and took them to Kilyos in Istanbul. They want history to disappear; they want to leave us without a past. But now there is a peace process; this is a new period. If peace is to be established between the Kurdish people and the state, between Kurds, Turks and Arabs, if there is to be peace, then no one’s past should be suppressed in this way. For this reason, we want to bring all our martyr comrades together. This issue, extending back to those from the earliest periods, including Şêx Seîd, Seyit Rıza and Geliyê Zilan, must also be resolved within the framework of this peace and resolution process. We know the whereabouts of most of our martyr comrades, particularly those who lost their lives from 2000 to the present day. We need to bring them all together. As for those whose names were recently announced, their families can rest assured that the remains of most of them, with perhaps only a few exceptions, are under our control.


We attach great importance to this issue. We are currently bringing them together and want to gather them all in cemeteries for our martyr comrades. We are working on this issue. We will not allow any of our martyr comrades to be lost. We are doing everything we can, and of course, we also ask for the assistance of those who have information. We want to bring all our martyr comrades together. They are the values and the history of this people. Their memory must belong to their society; they must not be lost. They must never be forgotten. This is how we must honour and protect the memory of our martyr comrades. As a people, we must embrace their legacy. We are the comrades of these friends; we live for them. The meaning of our lives is to fulfil their aspirations. Therefore, our priority is undoubtedly to safeguard the remains of our comrades and ensure that their memory becomes part of history. We are focusing on this issue; it is on our agenda. In brief, that is the situation.


There are calls for a national day of mourning. What would you like to say about these calls?


It is true that our people and our families are mourning and holding condolence gatherings. But from our perspective and in our approach, this is not mourning in the conventional, sombre sense. We mourn, but ours is a different …

title: Sultan Kara was not protected despite seeking help
content:
Three women have been killed and three others have died under suspicious circumstances in Diyarbakır (Amed) in the first eight months of this year. The city has now witnessed another femicide. On the evening of 26 August, Ersan Akdemir shot and killed 32-year-old Sultan Akdemir (Kara), from whom he was in the process of divorcing. Sultan Kara, who married four years ago, prepared a divorce petition two months ago in order to end the marriage. After deciding to divorce, she moved in with her sister. Kara was killed in Sümerpark in the Yenişehir district, where Akdemir had gone on the pretext of seeing their child. The perpetrator fled after taking the child from Fatma’s arms and has still not been apprehended. Şehriban Kara, the sister of Fatma Kara, spoke about the killing and said that Sultan had been subjected to systematic violence and death threats. She called for the perpetrator to be apprehended as soon as possible.


She filed for divorce two months ago


Sultan Kara was critically wounded at the scene and later died at the hospital where she was taken. She was laid to rest in Yeniköy Cemetery in the city centre. Kara was reported to have said after separating from the perpetrator, “I am very happy and at peace. I am free of him.” Sultan Kara had been subjected to violence throughout her marriage. On one occasion, she went to a police station seeking help but was reportedly sent away with the words, “Go to your own family’s home.” It also emerged that the perpetrator’s family repeatedly threatened her to prevent her from filing a complaint and that her daughter was taken away from her during this period as a means of intimidation.


Şehriban Kara summed up what happened to her sister with the words, “No one did anything.” Kara said, “My sister is dead, and we are all devastated,” adding that the perpetrator had also displayed similar behaviour in a previous marriage. She continued: “The state does nothing. Our sister is dead. She had been married for four years, and every morning my sister would say, ‘He is going to kill me.’ Twice, he beat her almost to death. He threatened her and assaulted her. Even when she was pregnant, he put his hands around her throat and tried to kill her.”


He threatened her every day


Şehriban Kara said: “His family threatened her so that she would not file a complaint. She filed a divorce petition two months ago and would say, ‘I am very happy, I am at peace. I am free of him.’ Along with the divorce petition, she had also requested a restraining order. After she decided to divorce him, the perpetrator threatened both my older sister and Sultan with death. My sister is dead, while that man is still walking around freely. Women are being killed and no one is taking this seriously. I want justice. Enough is enough!”

author: DebConf 25
title: Preseed your PBX for Fun and Profit
content:
by Chris Maj


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/147-preseed-your-pbx-for-fun-and-profit/


What is a PBX ?


Private Branch eXchange (PBX) systems connect desk phones in your school or office to outside lines from the telephone company. Over the past 25 years,

open source Asterisk-based systems like FreePBX

 replaced many proprietary competitors in phone closets around the world, by bridging calls between legacy analog copper lines, digital interfaces such as ISDN PRIs, and now ubiquitous Voice-over-IP (VoIP) solutions like SIP and WebRTC.


Why call a PBX an embedded application ?


PBX systems typically run around the clock, routing low latency audio streams and providing emergency calling capabilities to end users. Sangoma produces a line of hardware appliances, as well as cloud solutions, that offer curated FreePBX web interface experiences to help non-Linux users manage their systems effectively.


When did Sangoma start using Debian ?


For many years, Sangoma targeted CentOS for installations; but when the CentOS EOL date of July 2024 came up on the horizon, the decision was made to switch to Debian as the primary target for new FreePBX deployments. This overhaul involved migrating internal build pipelines and many pieces of custom code, including our ISO delivery mechanism.


Where is this talk going ?


During construction of the new FreePBX 17 Distro ISO, derived from Debian 12, we endeavored to make the install

as simple as possible

 using both existing

and potentially novel

 preseed customization ideas. Highlights of this talk will include:


Presentation of our GPLv2'd

Ansible role "

sngfd12

"

 for quickly generating a custom preseeded ISO based on the upstream stock Debian ISO as input.


Controlling expression of preseed selection at GRUB installer prompt using a unique

"spice level"

 concept.


Automatically partitioning, RAIDing, and resizing (sharing some clever insights

for partman fans

 😃


Novel approaches to

randomized password generation

 during installation - a topic particularly relevant to embedded application developers w/r/t ongoing regulatory changes in this area.

author: DebConf 25
title: The Role of Free Software and Debian in Green Sustainability
content:
by Mylena  Angelica


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/63-the-role-of-free-software-and-debian-in-green-sustainability/


This talk explores the pivotal role of free software, with a focus on Debian, in advancing sustainability within the technology sector. As digital infrastructures continue to grow, the environmental footprint of proprietary software becomes increasingly apparent. In this session, we will discuss how free software reduces the ecological impact of proprietary alternatives by promoting energy-efficient practices, longevity, and reuse. Debian, as an open-source project, not only minimizes the need for frequent hardware upgrades but also encourages more sustainable development practices in software creation and distribution.


The audience for this talk includes developers, open-source enthusiasts, and environmental advocates interested in understanding how technology can contribute to environmental sustainability. Attendees will gain insight into how Debian’s open-source philosophy aligns with green computing principles, helping reduce electronic waste and supporting long-term environmental goals. Key topics will include the advantages of using lightweight software, optimizing resource consumption, and how the community-driven nature of Debian fosters a culture of sustainability.

author: Taha Rezaei
title: Enchentes no Nepal e Tibete mostram que recuperação de desastres anteriores é crucial
content:
As inundações repentinas na fronteira entre Nepal e Tibete destruíram casas, estradas, pontes e projetos locais de geração de energia hidrelétrica. A inundação do rio Bhote Koshi está afetando 50 mil moradores. Mais de 500 pessoas morreram, e centenas estão desaparecidas, incluindo turistas estrangeiros.


Essa região do Himalaia ainda não havia se recuperado das inundações do rio Bhote Koshi em 2025, que mataram nove pessoas ao arrastar uma “ponte da amizade”

que ligava o Nepal à China

, interrompendo o comércio e o transporte por meses.


No Sri Lanka, as recentes inundações e deslizamentos de terra atingiram comunidades que ainda estavam se recuperando do ciclone Ditwah, que havia causado danos generalizados há nove meses.

Com pouco tempo

 para se recuperar do ciclone, as

comunidades

 ficaram sem proteção contra novas inundações. Mais de 15 mil pessoas foram diretamente afetadas e

6.800 pessoas

 foram deslocadas em agosto deste ano.


A

gestão do risco de desastres

 geralmente considera a intensidade da próxima inundação, incêndio florestal, ciclone ou seca. Mas os exemplos do Nepal e do Sri Lanka mostram duas dimensões que costumam ser negligenciadas:

quão rapidamente uma comunidade consegue

se recuperar

 e se isso acontecerá antes da chegada do próximo desastre.


Raramente um desastre deixa um lugar exatamente como ele era antes. E quando um segundo desastre acontece, estradas e pontes ainda podem estar danificadas, enquanto famílias já podem ter gastado suas economias. Empresas ainda podem estar em dificuldades. Governos podem continuar financiando a reconstrução, enquanto hospitais e outros serviços públicos permanecem sob pressão.


Se outro evento extremo ocorrer antes que esses sistemas tenham se recuperado, ele não encontrará a mesma comunidade que existia antes do primeiro desastre.

Encontrará um lugar com menor resiliência e

infraestrutura enfraquecida

.


Povoado no centro-norte do Nepal soterrado após inundações na fronteira com o Tibete


Uma maneira útil de compreender esse fenômeno é entender o chamado “intervalo de recuperação” (

recovery gap,

 em inglês): a relação entre o tempo necessário para a recuperação antes de outro

desastre capaz de causar danos

.


Imagine duas comunidades que passam por inundações semelhantes. Em uma delas, o último grande desastre ocorreu há dez anos. As casas foram reconstruídas, a infraestrutura foi reparada e os recursos de emergência foram repostos.


Na outra, o desastre mais recente aconteceu há seis meses. As estradas continuam em reconstrução, as famílias ainda estão deslocadas ou endividadas, e as autoridades públicas continuam pagando pela reconstrução. A nova inundação pode ser fisicamente semelhante nos dois locais. Suas consequências, porém, podem não ser.


Uma recuperação incompleta pode aumentar substancialmente as perdas no longo prazo.

 Um estudo de 2025 sobre inundações recorrentes nas Filipinas constatou que as perdas causadas por estas tragédias aumentaram

40% entre 2000 e 2018

 devido à recuperação incompleta.


Isso sugere que as perdas provocadas por desastres recorrentes nem sempre são simplesmente cumulativas.

O primeiro desastre pode alterar as condições em que o segundo desastre ocorre, fazendo com que os efeitos das tragédias subsequentes sejam muito mais graves.


A recuperação tem tempos diferentes


A recuperação costuma ser descrita como algo binário, como se uma comunidade conseguisse ou não se reerguer. Na realidade, trata-se mais de uma escala gradual.


O fornecimento de eletricidade e água potável pode ser restabelecido em poucos dias. Mas uma estrada danificada pode levar meses para ser reparada. A reconstrução de moradias pode levar anos. Empresas podem reabrir, enquanto ainda carregam dívidas substanciais.


As finanças das famílias, os ecossistemas e o bem-estar psicológico podem se recuperar em escalas de tempo completamente diferentes.


Assim, um lugar pode parecer recuperado de acordo com um indicador, mas continuar altamente vulnerável

de acordo com outro

.


Foram necessários mais de dez anos para que Nova Orleans, nos Estados Unidos, conseguisse se recuperar significativamente após o

furacão Katrina, em 2005

. Embora as operações básicas de emergência e o restabelecimento de energia tenham levado de semanas a meses, a reconstrução completa dos bairros, a estabilização da população e grandes melhorias no sistema de proteção contra inundações se estenderam por 15 anos ou mais. E isso em um dos …

author: Unknown
title: Ekvador'da eski Devlet Başkanı Moreno'ya rüşvetten 5 yıl hapis
content:
Fotoğraf: Agencia de Noticias ANDES/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 2.0

Ekvador’da eski Devlet Başkanı Lenin Moreno, ülkenin en büyük hidroelektrik santrali Coca Codo Sinclair’in inşasıyla bağlantılı yolsuzluk davasında suçlu bulundu. Mahkeme, 73 yaşındaki Moreno’yu Çinli Sinohydro şirketinden rüşvet almak suçundan 5 yıl hapis cezasına mahkum etti.

Mahkeme heyeti, yürüme engeli bulunan Moreno’nun cezasını cezaevinde değil, ev hapsinde çekmesine karar verdi. Mahkeme ayrıca eski Devlet Başkanı’nın kamu görevlerinden sürekli olarak men edilmesine hükmetti.

Moreno’nun fiziksel engeli nedeniyle cezaevine gönderilmeyeceği belirtildi.

Dava kapsamında Moreno’nun eşi, kızı, iki kardeşi ve diğer bazı aile üyeleri de suçlu bulundu.

Mahkeme, Moreno’nun eşi ve kızını 2 yıl 6 ay hapis cezasına çarptırdı. Aile üyelerinin de rüşvet ağına dahil olduğu sonucuna varıldı.

Ekvador’un en büyük hidroelektrik santrali olan Coca Codo Sinclair’in inşası, ülkede uzun süredir devam eden yolsuzluk tartışmalarının merkezinde yer alıyordu.

Çinli Sinohydro şirketine verilen milyarlarca dolarlık proje kapsamında rüşvet ödemeleri yapıldığı iddiaları uzun süredir soruşturuluyordu. Mahkeme, söz konusu ödemelerin Moreno’nun Devlet Başkanlığı döneminde gerçekleştiğini ve Moreno’nun rüşvet sürecinde aktif rol aldığını tespit etti.

author: DebConf 25
title: Mitigating kernel development bottlenecks and supporting the GNU/Linux ecosystem with kworkflow
content:
by David Tadokoro


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/62-mitigating-kernel-development-bottlenecks-and-supporting-the-gnulinux-ecosystem-with-kworkflow/


The Linux kernel project sits at the base of a gigantic and complex Free Software ecosystem. As a two-way road, downstream projects - the most prominent, Debian - feed off the kernel development while returning contributions to the upstream and giving it importance. Be it downstream or upstream development, if you work with the Linux kernel source code, chances are that you probably had to do one (if not all) of the following: set up a testing environment for custom kernels; fetching, optimizing, and managing several .config files; building a kernel from source; deploying a custom kernel to a testing environment. Before doing these tasks, some questions must be answered: Do I use physical machines or VMs as testing environments? What will the distro(s) of the target machine(s) be? Where do I get a base .config for a specific distro and architecture? What optimizations to do for building? How do I deploy the custom kernel to a particular testing environment?


For each combination of answers to these questions, surely, there will be a different sequence of commands, processes, paths to consider, and so on. After a few runs, you will probably be tired of manually doing all this work and will create scripts to automate your workflow. The problem is, if your workflow mutates a little or has slight variations, or your scripts have bugs, you will need to waste your precious development time maintaining these scripts that were not your objective in the first place! This is where

kworkflow

 (kw), a

Developer Automation Workflow System

 (DAWS), enters the scene. With a unified interface to many commands, kw abstracts many of these details, streamlines and automates time-consuming workflows, and enforces good practices so kernel developers can focus on the code they are writing, not on whether the make command was typed correctly.


Want to up a VM? Run kw vm --up;


Want to fetch a .config from within a machine in the network? Run kw kernel-config-manager --fetch;


How about compiling with optimizations and cross-compilation? Do some simple configuration with kw config, then just fire kw build;


I doubt installing custom kernels and modules is as simple as running one command, right? Wrong, you just need kw deploy.


In reality, kw does much more than this. For example, there is a

Terminal User Interface

 (TUI) feature to consult and manipulate patches sent to the mailing lists, resulting from a PhD applied research. This talk will introduce the key features of kw and show how it can be used to improve your kernel development workflows.


Even though kernel development has worked well for more than 30 years, we understand bottlenecks in developers' workflows are risking the long-term sustainability of the whole ecosystem, and projects like kw are vital to avoid this scenario beyond just automating tasks. At the end of the talk, we will want to collect feedback from the best community in the GNU/Linux distro world, the Debian community, about what kw is doing right and wrong and how the community experience and knowledge can help us have a more comprehensive view of the GNU/Linux ecosystem.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Unwavering, a mother of EJK victim confronts a decade of impunity
content:
The second truth-telling session of the Philippine Truth Commission hears the case of 17-year-old extrajudicial killing victim Darwin Hamoy and the search for justice of her mother, Mariza Hamoy on August 27, 2026. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

“It was easy for other people to tell me to give up the fight. But win or lose, I’ll never stop fighting. I’ll never lose hope for Darwin.”

MANILA – Mariza Hamoy, mother of extrajudicial killing victim Darwin Hamoy, has tried to go after the 16 police officers who killed her son. But her legal defeat has not deterred her search for justice, even once, even in the face of mounting threats.

“It was easy for other people to tell me to give up the fight. But win or lose, I’ll never stop fighting. I’ll never lose hope for Darwin,” she said in Filipino during the second truth-telling session of the Philippine Truth Commission, a civil society-led initiative to probe the “drug war” of Rodrigo Duterte, on Thursday, August 27.

Darwin and four of his friends were killed by the policemen in a buy-bust operation in Payatas, Quezon City, on August 15, 2016. He was 17 years old.

He was buying cigarettes for his friend William Bordios, also one of the victims, during a birthday celebration. It was the first “nanlaban” (drug suspect supposedly fought back) cases during the early years of Rodrigo Duterte’s anti-illegal drug campaign.

“My son was diligent, kind, and good at math…He was helping us work to sustain our family,” Hamoy said.

Hamoy was a street sweeper while her husband was a construction worker. Both were earning below the daily minimum wage then. “Our income was not enough. He [Darwin] was helping us buy rice and water for our daily needs,” she said.

When her son was killed, Hamoy did not immediately have access to his body. It took her eight days to find her son’s body in a funeral home in Quezon City. She was asked to pay P15,000 (US$240.72) to retrieve the remains. It took her a total of two weeks to get Darwin buried.

“I only had P2,000 (US$32.10) during that time. I told them if I could make a downpayment so I could bring Darwin home. I told them that I was a street sweeper. They refused,” Mariza recalled. “It was when I told them that I was contacting the media that they allowed me to make the downpayment. But they asked me for another P2,000 for his clothes to be used at the wake.”

Tearingly, she said that she could not afford to see Darwin for the last time with his old clothes. So she decided to buy a barong.

Hamoy filed two legal cases against the 16 police officers who came from the Quezon City Police District Station 6. A 2017 Reuters investigation revealed that 39 percent of the city’s killings from anti-drug operations can be attributed to the QCPD Station 6 police officers, who reportedly called themselves “Davao Boys” since they came from or near Davao.

The first case was filed through the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) in 2017, which was later endorsed to the Office of the Ombudsman for criminal charges. But a year later, the charges were dismissed because there was “no evidence that the police used excessive force,” according to former Executive Secretary Salvador Medialdea.

Philippine Truth Commission Chairperson Raul Pangalangan, who was also a former judge of the International Criminal Court (ICC), explained the use of excessive force. He said, “There were an overwhelming number of police, considering that the victims were unarmed.”

The second truth-telling session of the Philippine Truth Commission hears the case of 17-year-old extrajudicial killing victim Darwin Hamoy and the search for justice of her mother, Mariza Hamoy on August 27, 2026. Photos by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

The second case was filed before the Philippine National Police Internal Affairs Service (PNP IAS) in 2017. A year after, the PNP IAS filed charges of grave misconduct and grave irregularity against the 16 policemen in 2018. It was only this year that Hamoy was informed that the charges were dismissed.

Their commander, Lito Patay, was also charged with two counts of grave neglect of duty and one count each of less grave neglect of duty and simple neglect of duty by the PNP IAS due to his leadership at the time of Hamoy’s death. But Malacañang cleared him of charges in 2022, when Duterte was still in power.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 29 août
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 19 août déteste tous les soldats, ceux de tous les pays comme de toutes les religions. Et elle n'aime pas non plus les rois, les nazis ou les troupes d'occupation. Ce qu'elle aime, c'est la liberté.


1786 :

 Dans le Massachussets, insurrection paysanne de Shay contre la hausse des taxes et des impôts.


1900 :

 A Milan se tient le procès de Gaetano Bresci, l'anarchiste qui assassina le roi Umberto I. Il est condamné à sept ans de travaux forcés et sera retrouvé pendu dans sa cellule.


1943 :

 Les nazis dissolvent le gouvernement du Danemark occupé. En retour, les Danois-es coulent leur propre flotte militaire.


1944 :

 Insurrection slovaque contre les nazis.


1970 :

 A Los Angeles, la police attaque une manifestation de personnes originaires d'Amérique Centrale qui manifestaient contre la guerre du Vietnam, faisant trois morts.


1973 :

 En Angleterre, l'IRA place deux bombes à Solihull ainsi qu'une troisième dans les magasins Harrod à Londres.


2005 :

 La Nouvelle-Orléans est dévastée par l'ouragan Katrina et les quartiers pauvres sont délibérément laissés à l'abandon par les pouvoirs publics. Des milliers de personnes mourront.


2016 :

 A Neder-Over-Heembeek (Bruxelles), attaque incendiaire contre le centre de l'INCC (Institut national de criminalistique et de criminologie : une voiture bélier enfonce le portail jusqu'à l'aile des laboratoires et le feu est mis. Voir une

chronique

.

author: DebConf 25
title: ci.rocm.debian.net: a Debian CI with AMD GPUs, for AI/ML packages
content:
by Christian Kastner


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/182-cirocmdebiannet-a-debian-ci-with-amd-gpus-for-aiml-packages/


Much of number-crunching today is performed on GPUs. This especially applies to AI/ML-driven workloads. ROCm is AMD's open source software stack for general purpose GPU computing, challenging Nvidia's CUDA.


The Debian ROCm team's mission is to integrate and support ROCm on Debian to the point that using an AMD GPU (enterprise and consumer) for computation tasks is only an apt-get away. And with "support", we don't just mean packaging the libraries: we want to actually demonstrate just how well ROCm works.


To this end, we forked Debian's CI tools and bootstrapped our own environment with GPU support, currently featuring more than a dozen GPU architectures.

Our CI

 works exactly like Debian's

official CI

, except that we only look at the subset of packages linked to ROCm libraries.


In this talk, I'll present a brief overview of our CI, and the policy and technical challenges we faced bootstrapping it. I'll then show how contributors can adapt their packages to get coverage in our CI.

At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/59-kubernetes-in-debian-a-resurgence-from-the-ashes/


Last year, we talked about the first steps of bringing Kubernetes into Debian. Since then, the Debian Kubernetes Team has made big progress!


In this talk, I’ll share what we’ve achieved over the past year: new tools, important package updates, and a fresh upstream version that fixes many bugs and security issues (CVEs). We’ll look at how these improvements are helping Debian become a better home for Kubernetes users and developers.


I’ll also talk about what’s coming next and how you can get involved.


Let’s keep building something great together.

author: DebConf 25
title: Automating "downstream" Debian package builds and updates in CI
content:
by Matthew Vernon


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/119-automating-downstream-debian-package-builds-and-updates-in-ci/


The Wikimedia Foundation's infrastructure runs on Debian. We sometimes need to make local changes to packages provided by Debian, or to backport Debian packages from newer releases to run in our production environments. Wherever we've done this, we also need to be able to apply updates from Debian, particularly bug-fix updates from stable point releases or security updates.


We've developed tooling to do this automatically in our gitlab-based CI environment. This tooling can periodically poll Debian for updates, attempt to merge those updates with local changes, and then build the resulting package and upload it to our staging apt repository. Further, it uses a git-first workflow, which means users do not have to be familiar with complex quilt-based workflows to make changes to Debian packages and have them built in CI.


This talk will explain how this tooling works, and how it has made our lives easier. The tooling is Free Software, so it will also explain how it could be used outside of the Wikimedia environment; if you use Debian packages in your environment and sometimes need to modify or backport what Debian ships, this could be for you!

title: Future of archive-wide testing
content:
by Lucas Nussbaum


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/98-future-of-archive-wide-testing/


Over the years, Debian has grown many services and efforts to perform various kinds of tests on source or binary packages: archive rebuilds, autopkgtest &

ci.debian.net

, reproducible builds, lintian, piuparts, debcheck, etc, etc, etc. There are also efforts to provide integration within a salsa CI pipeline, infrastructure to manage those tests (such as debusine), and infrastructure to expose results to maintainers (UDD and Tracker). Various tools have also been built to organize such tests and assist with processing results.


After an overview (hopefully complete!) of the current state of things, the aim of this BoF will be to identify gaps, opportunities for convergence, share feedback about potential improvements to processes, etc.

author: DebConf 25
title: Optimizing the Debian packaging workflow for easier collaboration and fewer burnouts
content:
by Otto Kekäläinen


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/138-optimizing-the-debian-packaging-workflow-for-easier-collaboration-and-fewer-burnouts/


As a long-term Debian community member I am concerned about the

dropping number of active maintainers

. When I have asked friends of mine why they stopped contributing to Debian, many have shared their frustration with ineffective processes and slow progress which made them feel their time is not well spent. When mentoring new contributors I often see people struggling with outdated and fragmented documentation, and the challenge to learn how to doto common and simple tasks in Debian packaging the right way. There is also a clear gap between a generation of developers who prefer email and IRC based collaboration, and a generation that feel more productive with browser based rich interfaces.


In this talk I present how I navigate this landscape, and how I structure my collaboration to be effective with various people using many different workflows, while at the same time having a clear, tried and tested workflow for myself, and how I help my mentees to learn Debian community and package maintenance work effectively.

author: DebConf 25
title: Real-Time capabilities on Debian: Concept and practical use
content:
by Erwann Roussy


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/172-real-time-capabilities-on-debian-concept-and-practical-use/


As Linux increasingly powers embedded systems, industrial automation, and time-sensitive applications, real-time capabilities have become essential. This talk demystifies Real-Time (RT) on Debian: what it means, how it works, and how you can take advantage of it.


We will start by defining real time and how Linux can fit into its definition. A dive into the PREEMPT_RT patch set will follow, exploring how it transforms the kernel into a deterministic and low-latency platform.


The session will cover the current state of RT support in Debian. It will highlight the role of system configuration to achieve low latency and the tools to simplify this process (eg: tuned). We’ll discuss CPU isolation, IRQ affinity, scheduler tuning, and latency measurement tools such as cyclictest.


At last, we'll take a brief look at how real-time performance can be achieved inside virtualized environments.


Participants will gain practical insights into:


When and why to use an RT kernel


How to install and configure Debian for real-time performance


Tuning and benchmarking techniques


Real-world use cases of RT on Debian (robotics, audio, energy systems, etc.)


This talk is aimed at developers and system integrators interested in deterministic performance and low-latency systems running on Debian.

author: DebConf 25
title: Kali Linux: Delivery of a rolling distro at scale with Mirrorbits
content:
by Arnaud Rebillout


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/122-kali-linux-delivery-of-a-rolling-distro-at-scale-with-mirrorbits/


Kali Linux is a rolling Linux distribution based on Debian. Packages and images are distributed via a network of

community mirrors

, and a

redirector

 in front. In practice, it means that APT requests hit http.kali.org and get redirected to a mirror close-by for the actual download.


This talk is about the redirector. After 10 years of using

mirrorbrain

, Kali switched to

mirrorbits

 2 years ago. We're going to talk about this transition, present the mirrorbits project, and highlight some recent developments that made it suitable for a fast-changing repository such as a rolling Linux distro.


We will also talk about the operational side of things, after running it for 2 years in production: how much time does it cost to maintain this setup, what kind of machine is required to run the redirector, etc etc.


The audience for this talk: sysadmins for FOSS projects, and more generally anyone who want to know how FOSS can be delivered to a worldwide audience at scale

without

 a CDN. We also want to bring some data points for those who wonder what it would take to run a redirector for Debian again.

author: DebConf 25
title: Twisting Debian for running on Mobile Devices
content:
by Arnaud Ferraris


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/157-twisting-debian-for-running-on-mobile-devices/


Over the past 5 years, the DebianOnMobile and Mobian teams have worked towards making it possible to run Debian on (a few) smartphones and tablets. This includes packaging mobile-friendly software for Debian, but also requires significant infrastructure plumbing in order to generate ready-to-flash images for supported devices, with a strong focus on automation.


This talk will go through the tooling used by the DebianOnMobile team and Mobian, including Salsa CI-based pipelines, image generation scripts and stable kernel upgrades. Mobile devices being "just" another class of embedded devices, the speaker will also highlight how those tools and workflows could be applied to many different embedded systems, easing both hardware enablement and image generation.

author: DebConf 25
title: ArKanjo: a tool for detecting function-level Code Duplication in the Linux Kernel
content:
by David Tadokoro


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/202-arkanjo-a-tool-for-detecting-function-level-code-duplication-in-the-linux-kernel/


The Linux kernel's massive scale (+28 M LoC, +20 K contributors) presents unique maintenance challenges. Surprisingly, Code duplication remains a persistent issue in the kernel's codebase, which could hinder its evolution and patching. Academic approaches often focus on pairwise comparison of code artifacts, not directly applied for comprehensive codebase analyses. Other existing free software tools explored in practice frequently suffer from limited functionality, such as primitive textual matching, prove too narrow in scope, or fail to deliver effective results on complex, large-scale codebases. Existing solutions generally fail to address the Linux kernel's specific needs: (1) scalability to handle its size, (2) actionable results for developers, and (3) integration with kernel development workflows. This paper presents ArKanjo, a novel command-line tool for Linux kernel maintenance designed to detect and analyze function-level duplications. Released under the MIT license, ArKanjo employs a two-stage architecture consisting of a Preprocessor and a Query Responder that separates computationally intensive analysis from efficient querying for duplications within large codebases. Pivotal advantages of ArKanjo over existing solutions include: (1) optimization for C codebases with kernel-specific patterns; (2) preprocessing that enables rapid queries without redundant analysis; and (3) prioritization of duplicates that impact maintainability, such as copied buggy logic. We evaluate Arkanjo against real-world duplication cases in recent kernel versions, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying problematic clones that generic tools often overlook. By identifying well-defined, manageable duplication instances, ArKanjo effectively lowers the barrier for new contributors, a capability evidenced by its role in guiding students to make their first code improvements to the kernel. ArKanjo offers immediate value to kernel maintainers and serves as a replicable model for clone detection in other large-scale free software projects.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Winnipeg security provider introduces its first Indigenous ambassador amid tensions
content:
Although she wears a uniform, the newest line of security at a downtown Winnipeg dollar store is armed with nothing but sage and understanding.


Viv Ketchum is

Impact Security Group

’s first Indigenous community ambassador. She has walked the aisles of the Dollarama at 295 Portage Ave., which she referred to as “the worst in the city,” six days a week, eight hours a day for the last month.


“I want to leave something behind,” she said. “I can come up to a big, huge guy [and ask him] to leave the store. It’s just the way I handle them. I do have training in that, but I also have life skills.”


Impact, a security services provider which serves a number of retail and post-secondary clients in the city, has been in operation since 2014.


According to Ron D’Errico, Impact’s president and CEO, Ketchum will be the first of many ambassadors, which are being introduced alongside “culture sensitive training” for existing staff.


Ketchum, a community figure and residential school survivor, works differently from a regular security officer. Her uniform is a black t-shirt with a Medicine Wheel printed on the chest and back. Although she helps deescalate situations which call for security intervention, she also looks after kids and aims to create a safe, nurturing environment.


She said people have called her “Sheriff Kookum,” which she thought was “ridiculous.”


D’Errico said he had been seeking culturally informed training for quite some time, and had already tried out a pilot program featuring ambassadors in March, although they were younger.


“It’s something that we’ve decided to take a look at in light of racial profiling by security guards in our company and other companies, as well,” he said, adding that the new programming has been working thus far, and he’s witnessed less violence as a result.


There is no set date on when the next ambassadors will hit the floor yet, but D’Errico said the Dollarama has already been “night and day.”


“[Ketchum] has been good with the community,” D’Errico said. “She’s very proud and transparent in her beliefs, and she holds me accountable in how we run our company.”


The decision to add Ketchum to the security roster at the Portage Avenue Dollarama location was a direct result of an incident which occurred on Feb. 28, when an Impact security guard assaulted a shoplifter, who was Indigenous, with brass knuckles.


The next day, several members of the community, Ketchum included,

formed a protest in front of the store

 to blow the whistle on racial profiling by security guards, which many Indigenous Peoples in Winnipeg were already used to.


In June,

APTN Investigates reported

 that the

Canadian Academy of Guard Training

, the module used to teach security guards in Manitoba, had not been updated in 20 years and features no mention of Canada’s history with Indigenous Peoples and cultures.


Impressions are “usually based on past experience, bias or attitude,” the module stated. “This seems to be a human trait and there is little we can do about our immediate reaction to people. But we can discipline ourselves to be fair in our dealings with people in spite of our personal prejudice.”


Ketchum said she was hesitant at first because of past experiences with security guards, but wanted to begin creating change.


“I walked the talk,” Ketchum said. “That means, I was one of the protesters and I was very impacted by what I saw in that video, but then I also told myself… there’s a lot of people saying, ‘if only I was there, I would have done something.’ Well, now I am doing something. I’m stepping up and creating change. That’s what I do.”


The job is hard work, Ketchum said, and hard on the knees — but she “loves it.”


“I do love the work,” she said. “I love the people, the retail staff. The cashier says, ‘Do you know everybody in the community? Because people come in and say, ‘Hi, Viv,’ and then they give me a hug.”


The uniform can be intimidating at first, but many people have changed their attitude once she begins to interact with them, she said.


“When we apprehend a shoplifter, I do make sure to tell them that I’m here to make sure that you’re okay,” Ketchum continued. “And I’ve had some incidents where the people around me say, we should be harassing the shoplifter. Then I step in and I explain, I’m there to make sure the shoplifter is okay, security guards are okay, and that you’re safe. by Samuel Henrique

How Debian handles security vulnerabilities (CVEs) for its packages.


Learn how security vulnerabilities are tracked and fixed, together with some tips on how to investigate things yourself, common mistakes, and good practices to follow to keep your Debian secure.


This talk is focused on the handling of security vulnerabilities for Debian’s packages.


There is some similarity to my talk “Fixing CVEs on Debian: Everything you probably know already” from DebCon24, but this talk is targeted towards users and system administrators instead, it doesn’t go into details on how to develop the fix.


Given the way distributions handle security vulnerabilities being very similar, this talk is a nice introduction to overall cybersecurity.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Indigenous leaders condemn Trump’s move to rename Lake Ontario
content:
Indigenous leaders and advocates are outraged after U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America.


The name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat word Ontari:io, which means “the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.”


Prime Minister Mark Carney pointed to that origin on Thursday and said the lake will be known as Lake Ontario “then, now and always.”


Wendat Nation

 Grand Chief Pierre Picard told The Canadian Press his nation was “shocked” to hear about Trump’s renaming of Lake Ontario, calling it an attempt to eradicate their history in the region.


The Wendat occupied parts of the St. Lawrence Valley to the Great Lakes, as the area was rich with both pre- and post-contact trade routes. They named the lake “Ontari:io.”


Its name predates the founding of both Canada and the United States.


Picard said he requested a meeting with U.S. Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra to talk about Trump’s move and one will be scheduled for next week.


“I want to tell him that it is unacceptable for us, as a nation, to have a president who can eradicate our history, our culture and our identity,” Picard said. “I don’t think anyone is able to change Trump’s mind, but for us it’s important for me as grand chief to bring our voice to the United States and tell them we are very upset with the decision.”


Picard said he hopes mapping companies do not comply with the unilateral name change from Trump, and that he has been told by Carney that Canada won’t either.


American mapping company MapQuest posted on social media Thursday that it’s not changing the name of Lake Ontario. In the post, the company directed people to a website where they could choose their own name for the body of water, sharing a picture with the example “Lake Are We Doing This Again?”


Trump’s move has been heavily ridiculed. Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers, a Democrat, posted a video of himself at a McDonalds restaurant, signing a fast food napkin to decree Lake Michigan would now be called “Lake Wisconsin.”


“See, I can sign napkins that say things, too,” Evers wrote on X.


The city council in Rochester, NY, the largest American city on the lake, passed a proclamation on Friday unanimously condemning Trump’s move and declaring Rochester will continue to use the Lake Ontario name.


“No serious person from the Native Tribes or U.S. and Canadian cities which share the lake, will ever call Lake Ontario ‘Lake America,’ the proclamation reads.


“This desperate and flaccid stunt by the President is a clear distraction from the issues that matter most to U.S. voters: the failing economy, housing, affordability and, lest we forget, President Trump’s unwanted and unwarranted war with Iran,” the proclamation said.


Trump directed all arms of the federal government to start calling it Lake America.


On Thursday, Trump pointed to his decision in 2025 to sign an executive order changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, and mused that maybe next he’ll change the name of the Atlantic or Pacific oceans.


Mohawk policy analyst Russ Diabo called the change “totally asinine,” and said it’s typical of Trump’s “racism towards anything Indigenous.”


If there’s any bright side to Trump’s action, Picard said it’s that Canadians now know where the name Lake Ontario really comes from — not the province, but his people.


“We’re proud of that, for sure,” he said.


Read more:


Who gets to name a lake? What to know about Trump’s renaming of Lake Ontario

Indigenous leaders condemn Trump’s move to rename Lake Ontario

APTN News

content:
Mücteba Hamaney | Fotoğraf: ANKA

İran lideri Hamaney, "Hükümet Haftası" vesilesiyle bir mesaj yayımladı.

ABD-İsrail planları, yaptırımlar ve ablukaya rağmen İran hükümetinin ortaya koyduğu çabaları takdir eden Hamaney, hükümeti enflasyon, işsizlik, piyasa yönetimi, büyüme, yatırım, yerli üretimi artırma ve İran ekonomisinde ABD dolarının rolünü azaltma konularına ciddi şekilde odaklanmaya çağırdı.

Tüm yetkililerin milli birlik ve toplumsal uyumun korunmasına öncelik vermesi gerektiğini belirten Hamaney, "Şüphesiz ki, geçmişte sevgili halkımıza doğrudan veya dolaylı zarar veren milli ve kamusal güdüleri zayıflatan ve hayali ikilikler, örneğin savaş veya müzakere, uzlaşma veya aşırıcılık, taviz veya savaş kışkırtıcılığı gibi söylemler, bundan sonra da aynı etkiye sahip olabilir. Bu nedenle, toplumsal uyuma zarar veren her türlü eylemin kesinlikle yasak olduğunu ilan ediyorum." ifadelerini kullandı.

Hamaney, "zayıflıkların ve eksiklerin" açıkça vurgulanmasının ülkenin düşmanlarına fayda sağlayabileceği uyarısında bulunarak, İran’ın gücünün vurgulanmasının önemine değindi.

author: DebConf 25
title: Guix: From transparent and verifiable to long-term reproducible research?
content:
by Simon Tournier


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/201-guix-from-transparent-and-verifiable-to-long-term-reproducible-research/


What's Guix? A build system? A package manager? An operating system? A Guile/Scheme library? And why academics already in love with Debian might be interested by Guix?


Software plays a central role in scientific production since most of research results are the outcome of computational processes. Hence, the ability to verify research results and to experiment with methodologies, two core tenets of the scientific methods, require reproducible software deployment.


GNU Guix is a software deployment tool that supports reproducible software deployment. Guix features include user specific package installation, transactional upgrades and rollbacks, packing containers, virtual machine instantiation. And Debian and Guix can coexist concurrently on the same running system.


Here, we focus on two features of Guix. When scientific practitioners experiment with methodologies, they need the ability to replace one or more dependencies in the whole set of the dependencies; changing the version, configuration or compilation options, compiler, etc. Guix easily allows to create user customized packages and computational environment variants.


When scientific practitioners verify research results, they need all the source code and how this source code is transformed into binary. This transformation is captured by the Guix revision (snapshot) and easily available via the command `guix time-machine'. What if the source code becomes unreachable? Software Heritage comes in. Software Heritage is a long term, non-profit, multistakeholder initiative with the ambitious goal to collect, preserve and share all source code publicly available, and to our knowledge Software Heritage the largest publicly available archive of source code.


Could we connect Guix with Software Heritage? Yes! It makes Guix the first free software distribution and tool backed by Software Heritage, to our knowledge.


This presentation opens to some remaining challenges toward a better open and reproducible research; especially how package managers can help.
